articles.title: Hooking Product Saves So Admin, Import, and REST All Agree
articles.excerpt: A product change made in admin, over REST, through CSV import, and through mass attribute update reaches four different code paths. This article maps them and wires one recorder that catches all four.
articles.content:
A merchant asked for a simple thing: every time a product's price or status changes, push the SKU to the PIM. The first implementation was a plugin on ProductRepositoryInterface::save(). It worked in REST tests, passed QA, and then quietly missed every change the catalog team made through CSV import and the "Update attributes" mass action. Nobody noticed for three weeks.

The root problem is that "a product was saved" is not one event in Magento. There are at least four write paths, and each one exposes a different hook. Before choosing a plugin, observer, or preference, you need to know which paths your requirement actually covers.

The four write paths

PathWhat runsHook that sees it
REST / service codeProductRepository::save() → resource model saveRepository plugin, catalog_product_save_after
Admin product formAdmin save controller → model/resource savecatalog_product_save_after (repository plugin only if your version's controller calls the repository)
System → Import (CSV)Direct multi-row SQL in Magento\CatalogImportExport\Model\Import\Productcatalog_product_import_bunch_save_after
Mass "Update attributes"Magento\Catalog\Model\Product\Action::updateAttributes()catalog_product_attribute_update_before

The model event catalog_product_save_after is dispatched by the abstract model's save cycle, so it fires whenever a product model is persisted through the resource model, including through the repository. That makes it a wider net than a repository plugin. Import and mass update never instantiate a product model per row, so neither hook sees them. That is by design: those paths are fast precisely because they skip the model layer.

So the decision is not "plugin or observer". It is "one observer for model saves, plus one hook per bulk path, all feeding the same service".

Why not a preference or a plugin on the resource model

A preference on Magento\Catalog\Model\ResourceModel\Product would catch model saves but still miss import and mass update, and it conflicts with any other extension that prefers the same class. A plugin on the resource model's save() has the same coverage as the observer with more coupling. The observer wins on coverage per line of code, and the bulk paths need their own handling anyway because they deliver IDs or SKUs, not models.

The module

The recorder writes changed SKUs into a small table. A cron or consumer can drain that table toward the PIM later; that part is out of scope here. Recording synchronously into a table keeps the save path cheap and survives PIM outages.

app/code/MaheshDave/ProductAudit/registration.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

use Magento\Framework\Component\ComponentRegistrar;

ComponentRegistrar::register(ComponentRegistrar::MODULE, 'MaheshDave_ProductAudit', __DIR__);

app/code/MaheshDave/ProductAudit/etc/module.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Module/etc/module.xsd">
    <module name="MaheshDave_ProductAudit">
        <sequence>
            <module name="Magento_Catalog"/>
            <module name="Magento_CatalogImportExport"/>
        </sequence>
    </module>
</config>

app/code/MaheshDave/ProductAudit/etc/db_schema.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<schema xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Setup/Declaration/Schema/etc/schema.xsd">
    <table name="maheshdave_product_change" resource="default" engine="innodb" comment="Changed product SKUs pending export">
        <column xsi:type="varchar" name="sku" length="64" nullable="false" comment="SKU"/>
        <column xsi:type="varchar" name="source" length="32" nullable="false" comment="Write path"/>
        <column xsi:type="timestamp" name="changed_at" nullable="false" default="CURRENT_TIMESTAMP" on_update="true" comment="Last change"/>
        <constraint xsi:type="primary" referenceId="PRIMARY">
            <column name="sku"/>
        </constraint>
    </table>
</schema>

The SKU is the primary key on purpose. Ten saves of the same product between two export runs collapse into one row, which is the behavior the PIM wants.

app/code/MaheshDave/ProductAudit/Model/ChangeRecorder.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\ProductAudit\Model;

use Magento\Framework\App\ResourceConnection;

class ChangeRecorder
{
    private const TABLE = 'maheshdave_product_change';
    private const CHUNK = 500;

    public function __construct(
        private readonly ResourceConnection $resource
    ) {
    }

    /**
     * @param string[] $skus
     */
    public function record(array $skus, string $source): void
    {
        $skus = array_values(array_unique(array_filter(array_map('strval', $skus))));
        if ($skus === []) {
            return;
        }

        $connection = $this->resource->getConnection();
        $table = $this->resource->getTableName(self::TABLE);

        foreach (array_chunk($skus, self::CHUNK) as $chunk) {
            $rows = array_map(
                static fn (string $sku): array => ['sku' => $sku, 'source' => $source],
                $chunk
            );
            $connection->insertOnDuplicate($table, $rows, ['source']);
        }
    }

    /**
     * @param int[] $productIds
     */
    public function recordByIds(array $productIds, string $source): void
    {
        $productIds = array_values(array_unique(array_map('intval', $productIds)));
        if ($productIds === []) {
            return;
        }

        $connection = $this->resource->getConnection();
        foreach (array_chunk($productIds, self::CHUNK) as $chunk) {
            $select = $connection->select()
                ->from($this->resource->getTableName('catalog_product_entity'), ['sku'])
                ->where('entity_id IN (?)', $chunk);
            $this->record($connection->fetchCol($select), $source);
        }
    }
}

insertOnDuplicate() with an explicit update column list means a repeat change only rewrites source; changed_at refreshes through on_update.

Wiring the three hooks

app/code/MaheshDave/ProductAudit/etc/events.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Event/etc/events.xsd">
    <event name="catalog_product_save_after">
        <observer name="maheshdave_product_audit_save" instance="MaheshDave\ProductAudit\Observer\ProductSaveAfter"/>
    </event>
    <event name="catalog_product_import_bunch_save_after">
        <observer name="maheshdave_product_audit_import" instance="MaheshDave\ProductAudit\Observer\ImportBunchSaveAfter"/>
    </event>
    <event name="catalog_product_attribute_update_before">
        <observer name="maheshdave_product_audit_mass_update" instance="MaheshDave\ProductAudit\Observer\MassAttributeUpdate"/>
    </event>
</config>

This file lives in global etc/, not etc/adminhtml/. Import can run from cron or CLI-based tooling, and REST runs in the webapi_rest area; an admin-only file would miss both.

app/code/MaheshDave/ProductAudit/Observer/ProductSaveAfter.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\ProductAudit\Observer;

use Magento\Catalog\Api\Data\ProductInterface;
use Magento\Framework\Event\Observer;
use Magento\Framework\Event\ObserverInterface;
use MaheshDave\ProductAudit\Model\ChangeRecorder;

class ProductSaveAfter implements ObserverInterface
{
    private const WATCHED = ['price', 'status', 'name', 'special_price'];

    public function __construct(
        private readonly ChangeRecorder $recorder
    ) {
    }

    public function execute(Observer $observer): void
    {
        $product = $observer->getEvent()->getProduct();
        if (!$product instanceof ProductInterface) {
            return;
        }

        if ($product->isObjectNew() || $this->hasWatchedChange($product)) {
            $this->recorder->record([(string) $product->getSku()], 'model_save');
        }
    }

    private function hasWatchedChange(ProductInterface $product): bool
    {
        foreach (self::WATCHED as $code) {
            if ($product->dataHasChangedFor($code)) {
                return true;
            }
        }

        return false;
    }
}

dataHasChangedFor() compares against the original data loaded with the model. A product saved without loading first (a bare model with only an ID and one attribute) reports every set field as changed, which errs toward recording too much. That is the right failure direction for a sync.

app/code/MaheshDave/ProductAudit/Observer/ImportBunchSaveAfter.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\ProductAudit\Observer;

use Magento\Framework\Event\Observer;
use Magento\Framework\Event\ObserverInterface;
use MaheshDave\ProductAudit\Model\ChangeRecorder;

class ImportBunchSaveAfter implements ObserverInterface
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly ChangeRecorder $recorder
    ) {
    }

    public function execute(Observer $observer): void
    {
        $bunch = (array) $observer->getEvent()->getBunch();
        $skus = [];
        foreach ($bunch as $row) {
            if (!empty($row['sku'])) {
                $skus[] = (string) $row['sku'];
            }
        }

        $this->recorder->record($skus, 'import');
    }
}

The import adapter dispatches this event once per bunch with the raw rows. Rows that only touch an attribute the PIM ignores will still be recorded; filtering by column here is possible, but import rows only contain the columns present in the CSV, so you would check array_key_exists() against your watched codes.

app/code/MaheshDave/ProductAudit/Observer/MassAttributeUpdate.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\ProductAudit\Observer;

use Magento\Framework\Event\Observer;
use Magento\Framework\Event\ObserverInterface;
use MaheshDave\ProductAudit\Model\ChangeRecorder;

class MassAttributeUpdate implements ObserverInterface
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly ChangeRecorder $recorder
    ) {
    }

    public function execute(Observer $observer): void
    {
        $event = $observer->getEvent();
        $productIds = (array) $event->getData('product_ids');
        $attributes = array_keys((array) $event->getData('attributes_data'));

        if (array_intersect($attributes, ['price', 'status', 'name', 'special_price']) === []) {
            return;
        }

        $this->recorder->recordByIds($productIds, 'mass_update');
    }
}

This is a before event, so a failed update would still leave rows behind. For a sync queue that is acceptable: the exporter sends current values, and an unchanged product produces a harmless no-op on the PIM side. If your downstream cannot tolerate that, record in a plugin on afterUpdateAttributes() of Magento\Catalog\Model\Product\Action instead.

On large stores the admin mass update may run asynchronously through the product_action_attribute.update consumer. The event still fires, just inside the consumer process, which is one more reason the observer config belongs in global scope.

Paths this still does not cover

  • Direct SQL from other extensions or ERP connectors that write catalog_product_entity_decimal themselves.
  • Scheduled changes in Adobe Commerce (staging) that become active at a time boundary rather than through a save.
  • Price changes produced by catalog price rules, which live in the index, not on the product.

If any of those matter, the honest answer is a database-level approach: an mview subscription on the attribute tables feeding a custom indexer, which captures writes regardless of who made them.

Checking each path

bin/magento module:enable MaheshDave_ProductAudit
bin/magento setup:upgrade
bin/magento setup:di:compile
bin/magento cache:flush

Then exercise one path at a time and look at the source column:

curl -s -X PUT "https://example.test/rest/default/V1/products/24-MB01" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"product":{"price":39.00}}'
SELECT sku, source, changed_at
FROM maheshdave_product_change
ORDER BY changed_at DESC
LIMIT 10;

Expected: model_save for REST and the admin form, import after a CSV import of a few SKUs, and mass_update after "Update attributes" on a price or status change. If the admin form produces no row, check that the attribute you edited is in WATCHED before suspecting the event.

articles.title: Loading Extension Attributes in getList() Without N+1 Queries
articles.excerpt: An afterGet plugin that loads one extension attribute is fine for a single order and turns into hundreds of queries on getList(). Here is the batched version, with a query-log check to prove it.
articles.content:
The usual extension attribute tutorial adds an afterGet() plugin, loads the value, and sets it. Then someone copies the same per-item lookup into afterGetList(), the ERP polls /V1/orders with a page size of 200, and every poll costs 200 extra queries. The response still looks correct, which is why this survives code review.

This article builds an erp_reference extension attribute on orders, stored in its own table, and loads it for list calls with one query per page.

Where the value lives

Putting a custom column on sales_order is tempting, but it makes the order table wider for every query in the system and it ties your schema to a core table's lifecycle. A side table keyed by order_id keeps the data owned by the module and lets you drop the module cleanly.

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderErp/registration.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

use Magento\Framework\Component\ComponentRegistrar;

ComponentRegistrar::register(ComponentRegistrar::MODULE, 'MaheshDave_OrderErp', __DIR__);

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderErp/etc/module.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Module/etc/module.xsd">
    <module name="MaheshDave_OrderErp">
        <sequence>
            <module name="Magento_Sales"/>
        </sequence>
    </module>
</config>

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderErp/etc/db_schema.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<schema xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Setup/Declaration/Schema/etc/schema.xsd">
    <table name="maheshdave_order_erp" resource="sales" engine="innodb" comment="ERP references for orders">
        <column xsi:type="int" name="order_id" unsigned="true" nullable="false" comment="Order ID"/>
        <column xsi:type="varchar" name="erp_reference" length="64" nullable="false" comment="ERP document number"/>
        <constraint xsi:type="primary" referenceId="PRIMARY">
            <column name="order_id"/>
        </constraint>
        <constraint xsi:type="foreign" referenceId="MAHESHDAVE_ORDER_ERP_ORDER_ID_SALES_ORDER_ENTITY_ID"
                    table="maheshdave_order_erp" column="order_id"
                    referenceTable="sales_order" referenceColumn="entity_id" onDelete="CASCADE"/>
    </table>
</schema>

resource="sales" matters if the project ever uses split databases (Adobe Commerce only, deprecated in 2.4.2 but still present in older installs). On a single database it resolves to the default connection.

Declaring the attribute

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderErp/etc/extension_attributes.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Api/etc/extension_attributes.xsd">
    <extension_attributes for="Magento\Sales\Api\Data\OrderInterface">
        <attribute code="erp_reference" type="string"/>
    </extension_attributes>
</config>

After setup:di:compile, the generated Magento\Sales\Api\Data\OrderExtension gets getErpReference() and setErpReference(). Those methods do not exist until generation runs, so a stale generated/ folder shows up as "Call to undefined method" rather than as a missing value.

The XSD also supports a <join> child that asks the extension attributes join processor to add the column to collection queries. It only helps when the repository's getList() passes its collection through JoinProcessorInterface::process(), and that varies by repository and version. A plugin is explicit and behaves the same everywhere, so that is what I use for anything a downstream system depends on.

One query per page

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderErp/Model/ErpReferenceReader.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\OrderErp\Model;

use Magento\Framework\App\ResourceConnection;

class ErpReferenceReader
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly ResourceConnection $resource
    ) {
    }

    /**
     * @param int[] $orderIds
     * @return array<int, string> order_id => erp_reference
     */
    public function getByOrderIds(array $orderIds): array
    {
        $orderIds = array_values(array_unique(array_filter(array_map('intval', $orderIds))));
        if ($orderIds === []) {
            return [];
        }

        $connection = $this->resource->getConnection('sales');
        $select = $connection->select()
            ->from($this->resource->getTableName('maheshdave_order_erp', 'sales'), ['order_id', 'erp_reference'])
            ->where('order_id IN (?)', $orderIds);

        $pairs = $connection->fetchPairs($select);
        $result = [];
        foreach ($pairs as $orderId => $reference) {
            $result[(int) $orderId] = (string) $reference;
        }

        return $result;
    }
}

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderErp/Plugin/AddErpReferenceToOrder.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\OrderErp\Plugin;

use Magento\Sales\Api\Data\OrderExtensionFactory;
use Magento\Sales\Api\Data\OrderInterface;
use Magento\Sales\Api\Data\OrderSearchResultInterface;
use Magento\Sales\Api\OrderRepositoryInterface;
use MaheshDave\OrderErp\Model\ErpReferenceReader;

class AddErpReferenceToOrder
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly ErpReferenceReader $reader,
        private readonly OrderExtensionFactory $extensionFactory
    ) {
    }

    public function afterGet(OrderRepositoryInterface $subject, OrderInterface $order): OrderInterface
    {
        $this->apply([$order]);

        return $order;
    }

    public function afterGetList(
        OrderRepositoryInterface $subject,
        OrderSearchResultInterface $result
    ): OrderSearchResultInterface {
        $this->apply($result->getItems());

        return $result;
    }

    /**
     * @param OrderInterface[] $orders
     */
    private function apply(array $orders): void
    {
        $ids = [];
        foreach ($orders as $order) {
            $ids[] = (int) $order->getEntityId();
        }

        $references = $this->reader->getByOrderIds($ids);

        foreach ($orders as $order) {
            $extension = $order->getExtensionAttributes() ?? $this->extensionFactory->create();
            $extension->setErpReference($references[(int) $order->getEntityId()] ?? null);
            $order->setExtensionAttributes($extension);
        }
    }
}

Two details that bite in practice. First, getExtensionAttributes() can return null on orders built outside the repository, so the factory fallback is not optional. Second, the order repository caches loaded orders in an internal registry by ID; afterGet() runs on every call regardless, so the lookup repeats for repeated get() calls in the same request. If a hot path calls get() on the same order repeatedly, memoize in the reader.

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderErp/etc/di.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:ObjectManager/etc/config.xsd">
    <type name="Magento\Sales\Api\OrderRepositoryInterface">
        <plugin name="maheshdave_order_erp_reference" type="MaheshDave\OrderErp\Plugin\AddErpReferenceToOrder"/>
    </type>
</config>

Global di.xml rather than webapi_rest/di.xml: admin code, observers, and email templates read orders through the same repository, and a REST-only plugin produces "works in Postman, empty in the PDF" bugs.

Writing the value

Reading is half the contract. If the ERP writes back through POST /V1/orders with the extension attribute set, nothing persists it unless you add a save plugin. Most integrations I have seen write the reference through a dedicated endpoint instead, which keeps the order save path untouched. Whichever you choose, do not let the attribute appear writable in the API schema without a persistence path behind it; clients will send it and assume it stuck.

Proving the query count

bin/magento setup:upgrade
bin/magento setup:di:compile
bin/magento cache:flush
bin/magento dev:query-log:enable

Seed a reference for a known order:

INSERT INTO maheshdave_order_erp (order_id, erp_reference)
SELECT entity_id, CONCAT('SO-', increment_id) FROM sales_order ORDER BY entity_id DESC LIMIT 50;

Then request a page:

: > var/debug/db.log
curl -s -G "https://example.test/rest/V1/orders" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "searchCriteria[pageSize]=50" \
  | jq '.items[] | {increment_id, erp: .extension_attributes.erp_reference}' | head -20
grep -c "maheshdave_order_erp" var/debug/db.log

The grep should return 1 for the whole page. If it returns 50, something in the stack is calling get() per item after getList() (third-party plugins on the order repository do this more often than you would expect), and the fix is in that plugin, not yours.

bin/magento dev:query-log:disable

Leave the query log off outside the test; it writes every statement to disk.

articles.title: Virtual Types for Per-Integration Loggers and HTTP Clients
articles.excerpt: Three integrations writing to system.log with one shared HTTP client config is a debugging tax. Virtual types give each integration its own log file and timeouts with zero new PHP classes.
articles.content:
When an ERP sync fails at 2 a.m., the first question is "what did we send and what came back?" On many projects the answer is buried in var/log/system.log between cache warnings, payment debug lines, and two other integrations that also log to the default channel. The second question, "why did it hang for 60 seconds?", usually ends at a shared HTTP client with no timeout.

Both problems have the same fix, and it does not need a single new PHP class: virtual types in di.xml.

What a virtual type actually is

A virtual type is a named set of constructor arguments for an existing class. The object manager creates an instance of the real class with those arguments whenever the virtual name is requested. There is no generated class file and no inheritance; you cannot instanceof a virtual type and you cannot type-hint one. That is the point: the consuming class depends on Psr\Log\LoggerInterface, and configuration decides which logger it gets.

The alternative people reach for is a subclass of Magento\Framework\Logger\Handler\Base with a $fileName property. It works, but it is a PHP file per integration that exists only to hold a string.

The consuming class

The client below knows nothing about which log file or timeout it uses. It is written exactly as it would be with the default logger.

app/code/MaheshDave/ErpConnector/Model/ErpClient.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\ErpConnector\Model;

use GuzzleHttp\ClientInterface;
use GuzzleHttp\Exception\GuzzleException;
use Magento\Framework\App\Config\ScopeConfigInterface;
use Magento\Framework\Exception\LocalizedException;
use Psr\Log\LoggerInterface;

class ErpClient
{
    private const XML_PATH_BASE_URL = 'maheshdave_erp/connection/base_url';

    public function __construct(
        private readonly ClientInterface $httpClient,
        private readonly ScopeConfigInterface $scopeConfig,
        private readonly LoggerInterface $logger
    ) {
    }

    /**
     * @return array<string, mixed>
     * @throws LocalizedException
     */
    public function ping(): array
    {
        $baseUrl = rtrim((string) $this->scopeConfig->getValue(self::XML_PATH_BASE_URL), '/');
        if ($baseUrl === '') {
            throw new LocalizedException(__('ERP base URL is not configured.'));
        }

        $started = microtime(true);
        try {
            $response = $this->httpClient->request('GET', $baseUrl . '/health');
        } catch (GuzzleException $e) {
            $this->logger->error('ERP ping failed', [
                'url' => $baseUrl . '/health',
                'error' => $e->getMessage(),
                'elapsed_ms' => (int) ((microtime(true) - $started) * 1000),
            ]);
            throw new LocalizedException(__('ERP is unreachable: %1', $e->getMessage()), $e);
        }

        $result = [
            'status' => $response->getStatusCode(),
            'elapsed_ms' => (int) ((microtime(true) - $started) * 1000),
        ];
        $this->logger->info('ERP ping', $result);

        return $result;
    }
}

Guzzle is a dependency of magento/framework in 2.4.x, so GuzzleHttp\ClientInterface is available without adding a package. Depending on the interface keeps the class testable with a mock handler.

The wiring

app/code/MaheshDave/ErpConnector/etc/di.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:ObjectManager/etc/config.xsd">
    <virtualType name="MaheshDave\ErpConnector\Logger\Handler" type="Magento\Framework\Logger\Handler\Base">
        <arguments>
            <argument name="fileName" xsi:type="string">/var/log/erp_connector.log</argument>
        </arguments>
    </virtualType>

    <virtualType name="MaheshDave\ErpConnector\Logger" type="Magento\Framework\Logger\Monolog">
        <arguments>
            <argument name="name" xsi:type="string">erp_connector</argument>
            <argument name="handlers" xsi:type="array">
                <item name="file" xsi:type="object">MaheshDave\ErpConnector\Logger\Handler</item>
            </argument>
        </arguments>
    </virtualType>

    <virtualType name="MaheshDave\ErpConnector\HttpClient" type="GuzzleHttp\Client">
        <arguments>
            <argument name="config" xsi:type="array">
                <item name="connect_timeout" xsi:type="number">3</item>
                <item name="timeout" xsi:type="number">10</item>
                <item name="http_errors" xsi:type="boolean">true</item>
            </argument>
        </arguments>
    </virtualType>

    <type name="MaheshDave\ErpConnector\Model\ErpClient">
        <arguments>
            <argument name="httpClient" xsi:type="object">MaheshDave\ErpConnector\HttpClient</argument>
            <argument name="logger" xsi:type="object">MaheshDave\ErpConnector\Logger</argument>
        </arguments>
    </type>
</config>

A few things worth knowing about this file:

  • fileName is relative to the Magento root and starts with a slash, the same convention core handlers use for /var/log/system.log.
  • Magento\Framework\Logger\Monolog is Magento's Monolog subclass. Passing it a fresh handlers array replaces the default handlers, so these entries no longer appear in system.log or debug.log. Usually that is what you want. If ops alerting watches exception.log, add the core handler Magento\Framework\Logger\Handler\Exception as a second item.
  • The Guzzle constructor parameter is literally named $config, which is why the argument name is config. Argument names in di.xml must match parameter names, not types.
  • Virtual type names look like class names by convention only. Namespacing them under the module avoids collisions; two modules defining ErpLogger would silently override each other.

A second integration is configuration only

When the shipping carrier integration arrives, it gets its own handler, logger, and client by repeating the pattern with different names and a 30-second timeout for label generation. The carrier class does not change, and neither does the ERP config. That isolation is what makes virtual types worth it: tuning one integration's timeouts can no longer break another.

The tradeoff is discoverability. A developer reading ErpClient sees LoggerInterface and assumes system.log. I add the log file name to the module's README and keep all virtual types for a module in its global di.xml, never scattered across area files, so there is one place to look.

Exercising it

A small command makes the wiring testable from a shell.

app/code/MaheshDave/ErpConnector/Console/Command/PingCommand.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\ErpConnector\Console\Command;

use Magento\Framework\Exception\LocalizedException;
use MaheshDave\ErpConnector\Model\ErpClient;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Command\Command;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Input\InputInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Output\OutputInterface;

class PingCommand extends Command
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly ErpClient $erpClient
    ) {
        parent::__construct();
    }

    protected function configure(): void
    {
        $this->setName('maheshdave:erp:ping');
        $this->setDescription('Call the ERP health endpoint using the connector client');
    }

    protected function execute(InputInterface $input, OutputInterface $output): int
    {
        try {
            $result = $this->erpClient->ping();
        } catch (LocalizedException $e) {
            $output->writeln('<error>' . $e->getMessage() . '</error>');
            return Command::FAILURE;
        }

        $output->writeln(sprintf('HTTP %d in %d ms', $result['status'], $result['elapsed_ms']));

        return Command::SUCCESS;
    }
}

Constructor injection in a console command means the client and its whole dependency graph are built when bin/magento lists commands. For a light class like this that is fine. For commands with expensive dependencies, inject a Proxy (MaheshDave\ErpConnector\Model\ErpClient\Proxy in di.xml) so listing commands stays fast.

Register the command, alongside the virtual types, in the same di.xml:

<type name="Magento\Framework\Console\CommandListInterface">
    <arguments>
        <argument name="commands" xsi:type="array">
            <item name="maheshdave_erp_ping" xsi:type="object">MaheshDave\ErpConnector\Console\Command\PingCommand</item>
        </argument>
    </arguments>
</type>

app/code/MaheshDave/ErpConnector/etc/module.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Module/etc/module.xsd">
    <module name="MaheshDave_ErpConnector"/>
</config>

app/code/MaheshDave/ErpConnector/registration.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

use Magento\Framework\Component\ComponentRegistrar;

ComponentRegistrar::register(ComponentRegistrar::MODULE, 'MaheshDave_ErpConnector', __DIR__);

The module has no system.xml, so bin/magento config:set would reject the path. Set the base URL in app/etc/env.php, which is where an environment-specific endpoint belongs anyway:

'system' => [
    'default' => [
        'maheshdave_erp' => [
            'connection' => [
                'base_url' => 'https://erp-sandbox.example.test',
            ],
        ],
    ],
],
bin/magento module:enable MaheshDave_ErpConnector
bin/magento setup:upgrade
bin/magento setup:di:compile
bin/magento maheshdave:erp:ping
tail -n 5 var/log/erp_connector.log

A healthy run prints something like HTTP 200 in 84 ms and writes a line tagged erp_connector.INFO: ERP ping. Point the base URL at a blackholed address (for example a non-routable IP) and the command should fail after about three seconds with the connect timeout, not after PHP's default socket timeout. That three-second failure is the real test that the client virtual type was injected.

If the log line lands in system.log instead, the logger argument did not apply. The usual cause is a typo in the argument name, which the object manager ignores silently, or a stale generated/metadata in production mode.

articles.title: Declarative Schema: Renames, Drops, and the Whitelist File
articles.excerpt: Rename a column in db_schema.xml and Magento drops the old one and creates an empty new one. Remove a column and nothing happens. Both behaviors come from the whitelist file, and both are avoidable.
articles.content:
Two bug reports that look unrelated have the same cause. In the first, a developer renamed ref_code to external_reference in db_schema.xml; after deployment the column existed, but every value was gone. In the second, a developer deleted an obsolete column from db_schema.xml, ran setup:upgrade, and the column was still there a month later.

Declarative schema compares the XML to the live database and generates the difference. It cannot see intent. A rename looks exactly like "drop one column, add another", and a removal is only applied if Magento knows your module created that column in the first place. That second piece of knowledge lives in etc/db_schema_whitelist.json.

What the whitelist does

The whitelist records every table, column, index, and constraint the module has declared. During setup:upgrade, Magento only drops elements that appear in the whitelist but no longer appear in db_schema.xml. Anything not in the whitelist is assumed to belong to someone else (a legacy install script, another module, a DBA) and is left alone.

That explains both reports:

  • The removed column was never in the whitelist because the developer never regenerated it, so Magento refused to drop it. Correct, conservative behavior.
  • The renamed column was in the whitelist. The new XML no longer mentioned ref_code, so it was dropped, and external_reference was created empty.

The whitelist must be committed and regenerated whenever the schema changes:

bin/magento setup:db-declaration:generate-whitelist --module-name=MaheshDave_Loyalty

It is additive: generating it again after a removal keeps the old entry, which is exactly what lets the drop happen on the next upgrade. Do not hand-edit it to "clean up" removed names.

Renaming a column without losing data

The column element accepts an onCreate attribute. migrateDataFrom(old_name) tells Magento to copy values from the old column when it creates the new one, before the old one is dropped.

app/code/MaheshDave/Loyalty/etc/db_schema.xml before:

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<schema xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Setup/Declaration/Schema/etc/schema.xsd">
    <table name="maheshdave_loyalty_member" resource="default" engine="innodb" comment="Loyalty members">
        <column xsi:type="int" name="member_id" unsigned="true" nullable="false" identity="true" comment="Member ID"/>
        <column xsi:type="int" name="customer_id" unsigned="true" nullable="false" comment="Customer ID"/>
        <column xsi:type="varchar" name="ref_code" length="32" nullable="true" comment="External reference"/>
        <column xsi:type="varchar" name="legacy_tier" length="16" nullable="true" comment="Unused tier code"/>
        <constraint xsi:type="primary" referenceId="PRIMARY">
            <column name="member_id"/>
        </constraint>
        <constraint xsi:type="unique" referenceId="MAHESHDAVE_LOYALTY_MEMBER_CUSTOMER_ID">
            <column name="customer_id"/>
        </constraint>
    </table>
</schema>

After, with the rename and the removal:

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<schema xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Setup/Declaration/Schema/etc/schema.xsd">
    <table name="maheshdave_loyalty_member" resource="default" engine="innodb" comment="Loyalty members">
        <column xsi:type="int" name="member_id" unsigned="true" nullable="false" identity="true" comment="Member ID"/>
        <column xsi:type="int" name="customer_id" unsigned="true" nullable="false" comment="Customer ID"/>
        <column xsi:type="varchar" name="external_reference" length="64" nullable="true"
                onCreate="migrateDataFrom(ref_code)" comment="External reference"/>
        <constraint xsi:type="primary" referenceId="PRIMARY">
            <column name="member_id"/>
        </constraint>
        <constraint xsi:type="unique" referenceId="MAHESHDAVE_LOYALTY_MEMBER_CUSTOMER_ID">
            <column name="customer_id"/>
        </constraint>
    </table>
</schema>

Then regenerate the whitelist so it contains external_reference as well as the old names:

app/code/MaheshDave/Loyalty/etc/db_schema_whitelist.json (generated)

{
    "maheshdave_loyalty_member": {
        "column": {
            "member_id": true,
            "customer_id": true,
            "ref_code": true,
            "legacy_tier": true,
            "external_reference": true
        },
        "constraint": {
            "PRIMARY": true,
            "MAHESHDAVE_LOYALTY_MEMBER_CUSTOMER_ID": true
        }
    }
}

Leave onCreate in place after release. It only acts when the target column does not exist yet, so it is a no-op on databases that already migrated and still correct on any environment that lags behind, such as a developer restoring an old dump.

Renaming a whole table works the same way at table level with onCreate="migrateDataFromAnotherTable(old_table_name)". For very large tables this is a full copy inside the upgrade, so measure it on a production-sized dump before trusting it with a maintenance window.

Removing something another module declared

You cannot drop another module's column by omitting it, because it is not in your whitelist. The supported route is to redeclare the element in your own db_schema.xml with disabled="true". That applies to columns, indexes, constraints, and whole tables. Use it sparingly: disabling a core index to speed up imports, for example, is something you will have to defend during every upgrade.

See the SQL before running it

Two flags on setup:upgrade make schema changes reviewable and reversible:

bin/magento setup:upgrade --dry-run=1 --keep-generated
grep -n "maheshdave_loyalty_member" var/log/dry-run-installation.log

Dry run writes the DDL it would execute to var/log/dry-run-installation.log without touching the database. For the rename above, you should see an ALTER TABLE adding external_reference, an UPDATE copying from ref_code, and the drops of ref_code and legacy_tier. If the UPDATE is missing, the onCreate did not parse; check for a typo in the old column name.

bin/magento setup:upgrade --safe-mode=1

Safe mode dumps data from columns and tables about to be dropped into CSV files under var/declarative_dumps_csv/. If a drop turns out to be wrong, bin/magento setup:upgrade --data-restore=1 restores from those dumps after you put the element back in the XML. It is not a backup strategy, but it is a cheap safety net for a release that removes columns.

Things that still need a data patch

Declarative schema moves data only for the rename cases above. Changing a column type from varchar to int, splitting one column into two, or backfilling a new non-nullable column from logic are data problems. Declare the schema, then write a data patch that transforms values, and make the new column nullable until the patch has run everywhere. Trying to do it in one step produces a failed ALTER on the first row that does not convert.

Checking the result

SHOW COLUMNS FROM maheshdave_loyalty_member;
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, COUNT(external_reference) AS with_reference FROM maheshdave_loyalty_member;

Compare with_reference against the count of non-null ref_code values you recorded before the deploy. Recording that number is the step people skip, and it is the only way to prove the migration copied everything.

articles.title: A Custom Indexer with Mview Changelogs for Partial Reindex
articles.excerpt: A nightly full rebuild of a derived table was fine at 20k products and unacceptable at 400k. This custom indexer uses an mview subscription so only rows touched since the last cron run are recalculated.
articles.content:
A category listing needed "approved review count" as a sortable value. The first implementation recalculated a summary table from a nightly cron with a TRUNCATE and a big INSERT ... SELECT. At 20,000 products nobody cared. At 400,000 products with marketplaces feeding reviews all day, the table was wrong for most of the day and the rebuild locked it for minutes.

Magento already has the machinery for "recalculate only what changed": an indexer with an mview subscription. Triggers on the source table write changed IDs into a changelog, and the indexer_update_all_views cron job hands those IDs to your indexer. You write the calculation once, scoped to a list of IDs, and get both full and partial reindex.

The pieces

  • indexer.xml registers the indexer so indexer:status, indexer:reindex, and the admin Index Management grid know about it.
  • mview.xml declares which tables to watch and which column identifies the entity. Magento creates the changelog table and the triggers when the indexer is switched to "Update by Schedule".
  • One class implementing both Magento\Framework\Indexer\ActionInterface (full, list, row) and Magento\Framework\Mview\ActionInterface (changelog batch).

Module and target table

app/code/MaheshDave/ReviewIndex/registration.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

use Magento\Framework\Component\ComponentRegistrar;

ComponentRegistrar::register(ComponentRegistrar::MODULE, 'MaheshDave_ReviewIndex', __DIR__);

app/code/MaheshDave/ReviewIndex/etc/module.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Module/etc/module.xsd">
    <module name="MaheshDave_ReviewIndex">
        <sequence>
            <module name="Magento_Review"/>
            <module name="Magento_Indexer"/>
        </sequence>
    </module>
</config>

app/code/MaheshDave/ReviewIndex/etc/db_schema.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<schema xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Setup/Declaration/Schema/etc/schema.xsd">
    <table name="maheshdave_review_count_idx" resource="default" engine="innodb" comment="Approved review count per product">
        <column xsi:type="int" name="product_id" unsigned="true" nullable="false" comment="Product ID"/>
        <column xsi:type="int" name="approved_count" unsigned="true" nullable="false" default="0" comment="Approved reviews"/>
        <constraint xsi:type="primary" referenceId="PRIMARY">
            <column name="product_id"/>
        </constraint>
    </table>
</schema>

No foreign key to catalog_product_entity here. Index tables are disposable and rebuilt from source; a cascade would add lock contention on product deletes for no real benefit.

Registration and subscription

app/code/MaheshDave/ReviewIndex/etc/indexer.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Indexer/etc/indexer.xsd">
    <indexer id="maheshdave_review_count" view_id="maheshdave_review_count"
             class="MaheshDave\ReviewIndex\Model\Indexer\ReviewCount">
        <title translate="true">Product Approved Review Count</title>
        <description translate="true">Approved review count per product for sorting and badges</description>
    </indexer>
</config>

app/code/MaheshDave/ReviewIndex/etc/mview.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Mview/etc/mview.xsd">
    <view id="maheshdave_review_count" class="MaheshDave\ReviewIndex\Model\Indexer\ReviewCount" group="indexer">
        <subscriptions>
            <table name="review" entity_column="entity_pk_value"/>
        </subscriptions>
    </view>
</config>

entity_column is the column whose value is written into the changelog. For product reviews, review.entity_pk_value holds the product ID, so the changelog will contain product IDs directly. Choosing this column well is the main design decision in any mview setup: if the source table does not carry your entity ID, you either subscribe to a different table or translate IDs inside execute().

Status changes (pending → approved) update the same review row, so the trigger covers moderation too. Deleting a review fires the delete trigger with the old row's value, which is exactly what we need to decrement the count.

The indexer class

app/code/MaheshDave/ReviewIndex/Model/Indexer/ReviewCount.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\ReviewIndex\Model\Indexer;

use Magento\Framework\App\ResourceConnection;
use Magento\Framework\DB\Adapter\AdapterInterface;
use Magento\Framework\Indexer\ActionInterface as IndexerActionInterface;
use Magento\Framework\Mview\ActionInterface as MviewActionInterface;
use Magento\Review\Model\Review;

class ReviewCount implements IndexerActionInterface, MviewActionInterface
{
    private const INDEX_TABLE = 'maheshdave_review_count_idx';
    private const BATCH = 1000;

    public function __construct(
        private readonly ResourceConnection $resource
    ) {
    }

    public function executeFull()
    {
        $connection = $this->resource->getConnection();
        $connection->delete($this->resource->getTableName(self::INDEX_TABLE));
        $this->insertCounts($connection, null);
    }

    public function executeList(array $ids)
    {
        $this->reindexIds($ids);
    }

    public function executeRow($id)
    {
        $this->reindexIds([$id]);
    }

    public function execute($ids)
    {
        $this->reindexIds($ids);
    }

    /**
     * @param int[]|string[] $ids
     */
    private function reindexIds(array $ids): void
    {
        $ids = array_values(array_unique(array_map('intval', $ids)));
        if ($ids === []) {
            return;
        }

        $connection = $this->resource->getConnection();
        $table = $this->resource->getTableName(self::INDEX_TABLE);

        foreach (array_chunk($ids, self::BATCH) as $chunk) {
            $connection->beginTransaction();
            try {
                $connection->delete($table, ['product_id IN (?)' => $chunk]);
                $this->insertCounts($connection, $chunk);
                $connection->commit();
            } catch (\Throwable $e) {
                $connection->rollBack();
                throw $e;
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * @param int[]|null $productIds null means all products
     */
    private function insertCounts(AdapterInterface $connection, ?array $productIds): void
    {
        $select = $connection->select()
            ->from(['r' => $this->resource->getTableName('review')], [])
            ->join(
                ['re' => $this->resource->getTableName('review_entity')],
                're.entity_id = r.entity_id',
                []
            )
            ->where('re.entity_code = ?', Review::ENTITY_PRODUCT_CODE)
            ->where('r.status_id = ?', Review::STATUS_APPROVED)
            ->group('r.entity_pk_value')
            ->columns([
                'product_id' => 'r.entity_pk_value',
                'approved_count' => new \Zend_Db_Expr('COUNT(*)'),
            ]);

        if ($productIds !== null) {
            $select->where('r.entity_pk_value IN (?)', $productIds);
        }

        $connection->query(
            $connection->insertFromSelect(
                $select,
                $this->resource->getTableName(self::INDEX_TABLE),
                ['product_id', 'approved_count']
            )
        );
    }
}

Products whose last approved review was removed simply disappear from the table after the delete, and readers treat a missing row as zero. That is cheaper than writing zeros for 400,000 products on every full reindex.

The full reindex here deletes and rebuilds in place, so readers briefly see an empty table. For this data that is acceptable. If it is not for yours, core uses a replica-table swap through Magento\Framework\Indexer\Table\StrategyInterface; it adds complexity worth paying only when readers cannot tolerate a gap.

\Zend_Db_Expr is still what Magento\Framework\DB\Select expects for expressions in 2.4.x. Projects on 2.4.6+ may see it aliased through laminas packages; the class name used by core code remains Zend_Db_Expr.

Turning it on

bin/magento module:enable MaheshDave_ReviewIndex
bin/magento setup:upgrade
bin/magento setup:di:compile
bin/magento indexer:set-mode schedule maheshdave_review_count
bin/magento indexer:reindex maheshdave_review_count
bin/magento indexer:status maheshdave_review_count

Switching to schedule mode is what creates the changelog table maheshdave_review_count_cl and the triggers on review. In "Update on Save" mode nothing is subscribed, and since this indexer has no save hooks of its own, it would only change on full reindex. If you want realtime mode to work too, add an observer on review_save_after that calls executeRow(); for review volume I would not bother.

Watching a partial reindex happen

Approve a pending review in admin (or update one directly on a dev database), then:

SELECT * FROM maheshdave_review_count_cl ORDER BY version_id DESC LIMIT 5;
SHOW TRIGGERS LIKE 'review';

The changelog should hold the product ID with a new version_id. Then process the backlog the way production cron would:

bin/magento cron:run --group=index
bin/magento indexer:status maheshdave_review_count
SELECT * FROM maheshdave_review_count_idx WHERE product_id = 42;
SELECT version_id FROM mview_state WHERE view_id = 'maheshdave_review_count';

The count should reflect the approval, and mview_state.version_id should have advanced to the changelog's latest version. If the changelog grows but the state never moves, the index cron group is not running; that is a cron problem, not an indexer problem, and indexer:status will show the backlog as "N in backlog" on 2.4.x.

articles.title: One Queue Topic on MySQL Locally and RabbitMQ in Production
articles.excerpt: The same order-export topic should run on the database queue in DDEV and on RabbitMQ in production. Magento resolves that from env.php, as long as the XML does not pin a connection.
articles.content:
An order export that only runs when RabbitMQ is up will not run on a developer laptop, so people test it for the first time on staging. The inverse, a consumer hardcoded to the MySQL queue, sits idle in production after the broker is installed because nothing publishes to it. Magento already picks the transport at deploy time. The module should define the topic once and leave the connection unset.

Connection resolution, as documented for communication.xml, queue_publisher.xml, queue_topology.xml, and queue_consumer.xml: if you omit connection, Magento uses amqp when env.php contains an AMQP config, stomp when ActiveMQ Artemis is configured (2.4.5+), and db otherwise. Pinning connection="db" disables that. Pinning both and toggling disabled also works, but then every environment change is a code change. Omitting the attribute is the version I ship.

What gets published

The message is the order id as a string. A data interface is worth it when the payload has several fields; an id is enough here because the consumer reloads the order and therefore sees the current state rather than a snapshot that went stale in the queue.

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/etc/communication.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Communication/etc/communication.xsd">
    <topic name="maheshdave.order.export" request="string"/>
</config>

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/etc/queue_publisher.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework-message-queue:etc/publisher.xsd">
    <publisher topic="maheshdave.order.export"/>
</config>

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/etc/queue_topology.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework-message-queue:etc/topology.xsd">
    <exchange name="magento" type="topic">
        <binding id="maheshdaveOrderExport" topic="maheshdave.order.export" destinationType="queue" destination="maheshdave.order.export"/>
    </exchange>
</config>

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/etc/queue_consumer.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework-message-queue:etc/consumer.xsd">
    <consumer name="maheshdave.order.export" queue="maheshdave.order.export" handler="MaheshDave\OrderExport\Model\ExportHandler::process" maxMessages="100"/>
</config>

maxMessages="100" makes the process exit after a bounded amount of work so a supervisor or cron restarts it. Without a cap, a consumer that leaks memory lives until someone notices the RSS.

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/Model/ExportPublisher.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\OrderExport\Model;

use Magento\Framework\MessageQueue\PublisherInterface;

class ExportPublisher
{
    public const TOPIC = 'maheshdave.order.export';

    public function __construct(
        private readonly PublisherInterface $publisher
    ) {
    }

    public function publish(int $orderId): void
    {
        $this->publisher->publish(self::TOPIC, (string) $orderId);
    }
}

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/Model/ExportHandler.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\OrderExport\Model;

use Magento\Sales\Api\OrderRepositoryInterface;
use Psr\Log\LoggerInterface;

class ExportHandler
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly OrderRepositoryInterface $orderRepository,
        private readonly LoggerInterface $logger
    ) {
    }

    public function process(string $orderId): void
    {
        $order = $this->orderRepository->get((int) $orderId);
        $this->logger->info('Exporting order', ['increment_id' => $order->getIncrementId()]);
    }
}

Throwing from process() rejects the message and Magento retries it. Catching every exception and returning makes a poison message look successful. If the ERP is down, throw. If the order id is nonsense, log and return so it does not retry forever. That split belongs in this method once the real client exists; the handler above is the boundary, and a missing order throws NoSuchEntityException, which is the retry case I accept because a replica lag of a few seconds is normal right after placement.

Where the transport is chosen

Local app/etc/env.php has no queue/amqp key, so this topic uses the queue and queue_message tables. Production has the broker block Magento writes when you configure RabbitMQ (host, port, user, password, virtualhost). Do not commit that block. After changing it, bin/magento setup:upgrade recreates the queue topology for the resolved connection.

One explicit override is legitimate: a consumer that must stay on MySQL even in production, because it is a small control message and you do not want the broker as a dependency. Set connection="db" on that consumer and on its exchange only. Do not set it on this export.

Seeing it move

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/registration.php

<?php

ComponentRegistrar::register(ComponentRegistrar::MODULE, 'MaheshDave_OrderExport', __DIR__);

        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Module/etc/module.xsd">
    <module name="MaheshDave_OrderExport">
        <sequence>
            <module name="Magento_Sales"/>

</config>
bin/magento setup:upgrade
bin/magento setup:di:compile
bin/magento queue:consumers:list | grep maheshdave.order.export

Publish from a one-off integration test or by placing an order through a plugin on OrderRepositoryInterface::save that calls ExportPublisher only when the order is new. Then:

SELECT id, topic_name, body FROM queue_message ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5;

On a laptop this returns a row with topic maheshdave.order.export and the order id as the body, and the consumer log line follows. On production the same SQL returns nothing, because the row is in RabbitMQ; rabbitmqctl list_queues name messages (or the managed equivalent) shows maheshdave.order.export. articles.title: A Product Field in GraphQL That Does Not Query Once Per Item
articles.excerpt: A GraphQL product field that calls a repository inside the resolver runs one query per product on a listing. Resolve the whole page in one load and read the map from the field resolver.
articles.content:
A category page asks GraphQL for 24 products and a custom backorder_note field. The resolver loads a row by SKU. The page is correct and the database log shows 24 identical selects. GraphQL calls the field resolver once per item; Magento does not batch those calls for you unless the field is backed by a data loader you wrote.

The approach that holds up: the field resolver implements BatchResolverInterface, so Magento hands it every product on the page in one call. It loads those SKUs with a single IN (?) query and answers each item from the map.

Schema

This is a field on ProductInterface, not a new root query. Root queries you invent are outside the cacheable query list Adobe documents (products, categories, route, and the others on that page). A field on products rides the query that is already cacheable.

app/code/MaheshDave/CatalogNote/etc/schema.graphqls

interface ProductInterface {
    backorder_note: String @resolver(class: "MaheshDave\\CatalogNote\\Model\\Resolver\\BackorderNote") @doc(description: "Merchandising note when the product is on backorder")
}

app/code/MaheshDave/CatalogNote/etc/db_schema.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<schema xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Setup/Declaration/Schema/etc/schema.xsd">
    <table name="maheshdave_backorder_note" resource="default" engine="innodb" comment="Backorder notes by SKU">
        <column xsi:type="varchar" name="sku" length="64" nullable="false" comment="SKU"/>
        <column xsi:type="varchar" name="note" length="255" nullable="false" comment="Note"/>
        <constraint xsi:type="primary" referenceId="PRIMARY">
            <column name="sku"/>
        </constraint>
    </table>
</schema>

app/code/MaheshDave/CatalogNote/Model/NoteLoader.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\CatalogNote\Model;

use Magento\Framework\App\ResourceConnection;

class NoteLoader
{
    /** @var array<string, string>|null */
    private ?array $notes = null;

    public function __construct(
        private readonly ResourceConnection $resource
    ) {
    }

    /**
     * @param string[] $skus
     */
    public function warm(array $skus): void
    {
        if ($this->notes !== null) {
            return;
        }
        $skus = array_values(array_unique(array_filter($skus)));
        $this->notes = [];
        if ($skus === []) {
            return;
        }
        $connection = $this->resource->getConnection();
        $select = $connection->select()
            ->from($this->resource->getTableName('maheshdave_backorder_note'), ['sku', 'note'])
            ->where('sku IN (?)', $skus);
        foreach ($connection->fetchPairs($select) as $sku => $note) {
            $this->notes[(string) $sku] = (string) $note;
        }
    }

    public function get(string $sku): ?string
    {
        return $this->notes[$sku] ?? null;
    }
}

The loader is a normal injectable, so Magento gives you one instance per request. That is the memoization. Do not store this map on a singleton you registered yourself; the shared instance would leak the previous request's SKUs across PHP-FPM workers only if you made it static, and a static property here would survive for the life of the worker and serve another customer's catalog. Keep it on the object.

Magento 2.4.7 (and the 2.4 line that includes BatchResolverInterface) will call resolve() once with every parent product when the resolver implements that interface instead of ResolverInterface. Confirmed against lib/internal/Magento/Framework/GraphQl/Query/Resolver/BatchResolverInterface.php on the 2.4.7 tag. A class that implements the single-item interface never sees the rest of the page.

app/code/MaheshDave/CatalogNote/Model/Resolver/BackorderNote.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\CatalogNote\Model\Resolver;

use Magento\Framework\GraphQl\Config\Element\Field;
use Magento\Framework\GraphQl\Query\Resolver\BatchRequestItemInterface;
use Magento\Framework\GraphQl\Query\Resolver\BatchResolverInterface;
use Magento\Framework\GraphQl\Query\Resolver\BatchResponse;
use Magento\Framework\GraphQl\Query\Resolver\ContextInterface;
use MaheshDave\CatalogNote\Model\NoteLoader;

class BackorderNote implements BatchResolverInterface
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly NoteLoader $noteLoader
    ) {
    }

    /**
     * @param BatchRequestItemInterface[] $requests
     */
    public function resolve(ContextInterface $context, Field $field, array $requests): BatchResponse
    {
        $skus = [];
        foreach ($requests as $request) {
            $sku = (string) ($request->getValue()['sku'] ?? '');
            if ($sku !== '') {
                $skus[] = $sku;
            }
        }
        $this->noteLoader->warm($skus);

        $response = new BatchResponse();
        foreach ($requests as $request) {
            $sku = (string) ($request->getValue()['sku'] ?? '');
            $response->addResponse($request, $sku === '' ? null : $this->noteLoader->get($sku));
        }

        return $response;
    }
}

BatchResponse stores values in an SplObjectStorage keyed by the request object. You must pass the same $request instance you were given; a copy will not match and findResponseFor() throws when Magento reads the result back. getValue() is the parent array the product resolver already built, which includes sku for a ProductInterface field. It is null when the field is resolved without a parent, and the resolver returns null rather than querying.

registration.php registers MaheshDave_CatalogNote. etc/module.xml sequences Magento_CatalogGraphQl and Magento_GraphQl.

Proof

bin/magento setup:upgrade
bin/magento setup:di:compile
bin/magento cache:flush
bin/magento dev:query-log:enable
: > var/debug/db.log
query {
  products(filter: { sku: { in: ["24-MB01", "24-MB04", "24-WG01"] } }) {
    items { sku name backorder_note }
  }
}
curl -s -G "https://example.test/graphql" --data-urlencode "query={products(filter:{sku:{in:[\"24-MB01\",\"24-MB04\",\"24-WG01\"]}}){items{sku backorder_note}}}"
grep -c "maheshdave_backorder_note" var/debug/db.log
bin/magento dev:query-log:disable

The count must be 1. A count of 3 means the plugin did not run (compiled DI is stale, or the plugin is in global di.xml but a preference replaced Products) or warm() is not short-circuiting. Seed the table first or every value is null and you will "fix" a loader that was fine.

articles.title: Why a GraphQL Query Never Hits Fastly
articles.excerpt: Apollo POSTs the products query, Fastly never stores it, and the cache-id header from the response is thrown away. GET, the documented cacheable query list, and X-Magento-Cache-Id are the actual levers.
articles.content:
The storefront team reported a Fastly hit rate near zero on /graphql while category HTML sat at 90%. The query was products, which Magento does cache. The client was sending it as an HTTP POST with the query in the body. Fastly's Commerce VCL only considers caching a GraphQL request when it is a GET whose query string contains query=. A POST is a pass, every time, and no Magento header will change that.

What Magento will cache

Adobe's GraphQL caching documentation lists the queries that participate: products, categories, categoryList, cmsBlocks, cmsPage, route, storeConfig, urlResolver, and a short set of metadata queries. It explicitly does not cache cart, customer, customerOrders, wishlist, or customer payment tokens. One uncached root field in an otherwise cacheable document bypasses the cache for the whole request. A persisted "page" query that also asks for customer { firstname } is a permanent miss, and it looks like a Fastly bug.

A custom root query you add in schema.graphqls is not on that list. I do not add one when the data can be a field of products or categories. Those parents already carry cache tags (X-Magento-Tags in developer mode), so a price change purges the response. A new root query would need its own cache identity wiring, and that wiring is not a documented one-liner; treat a claim that @cache on an arbitrary query "just works" as something to verify on your patch level before you depend on it.

The cache id is not the URL

From 2.4.4, Magento returns X-Magento-Cache-Id on GraphQL GET and POST responses. The value is a SHA-256 of store id, currency, whether the customer is logged in, customer group, customer tax rate, and a salt. Sending that value back on the next request lets Fastly (module 1.2.160 or later, with the current VCL uploaded) serve a different object per context without varying on the Authorization bearer or on cookies. The header is for Varnish and Fastly. The built-in file FPC does not honor it. Mutations do not return it.

Guest traffic does not need the header for a hit. Logged-in traffic does, because a bearer token would otherwise make every key unique. The client has to store the header from the response and attach it to the following GET. Most Apollo setups never do this, because they POST and never read response headers.

X-Magento-Vary is not used for GraphQL. Store and currency come from the Store and Content-Currency headers. A query with no Store header is cached under the default store, then replayed to a request for another store view if you vary only on the URL. I send Store on every request, including the ones I expect to hit.

A request that can hit

curl -sD - -o /dev/null -G "https://example.test/graphql" \
  -H "Store: default" \
  -H "Content-Currency: USD" \
  --data-urlencode 'query=query{products(filter:{sku:{eq:"24-MB01"}}){items{sku name}}}'

First response: X-Magento-Cache-Debug: MISS when the app is in developer mode, and Fastly's X-Cache contains MISS. Second identical request: HIT. The same call with -X POST and a JSON body stays on MISS or PASS. If the second GET is still a miss, check three things in order: the Fastly module is at least 1.2.160 and the VCL has been uploaded, the query string actually contains the query (a persisted-query POST will not), and the document does not include a field from the uncached list.

For a logged-in client, read X-Magento-Cache-Id from the first response and send it next time:

CACHE_ID=$(curl -sD - -o /dev/null -G "https://example.test/graphql" \
  -H "Store: default" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode 'query=query{products(search:"bag"){items{sku}}}' \
  | awk -F': ' 'tolower($1)=="x-magento-cache-id"{gsub("\r","",$2); print $2}')
curl -sD - -o /dev/null -G "https://example.test/graphql" \
  -H "Store: default" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Magento-Cache-Id: $CACHE_ID" \
  --data-urlencode 'query=query{products(search:"bag"){items{sku}}}'

The customer token still has to be valid; the cache id only stops Fastly from treating that token as part of the cache key. Group and tax rate are already inside the hash. If you add another factor through idFactorProviders on Magento\GraphQlCache\Model\CacheId\CacheIdCalculator, every distinct value multiplies the number of objects. I have used that for a B2B shared-catalog id, and the hit rate fell until the catalog count was small enough that the extra dimension paid for itself. Measure the cardinality before you add a factor, not after the Fastly bill moves.

articles.title: A REST Endpoint That Shares Its Service Contract with Cron
articles.excerpt: The cron job and the integration both need to mark an order as exported. A controller action only serves HTTP. A service contract is callable from both, and webapi.xml is just the HTTP binding.
articles.content:
Two features landed in the same sprint: an ERP that POSTs "this order is exported", and a cron that retries orders the ERP never acknowledged. Both were written as separate blocks of SQL. They drifted within a month, and the cron started overwriting a status the API had just set because it did not know about the new column.

The HTTP route is not the feature. webapi.xml binds a URL to a method on a service interface. Cron, a consumer, and an admin controller can call that method without HTTP. If the only implementation lives in a controller, the cron will grow a second copy.

The contract

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/Api/ExportStatusInterface.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\OrderExport\Api;

use Magento\Framework\Exception\NoSuchEntityException;

interface ExportStatusInterface
{
    /**
     * @param string $incrementId
     * @param string $state exported|failed
     * @return string
     * @throws NoSuchEntityException
     */
    public function setState(string $incrementId, string $state): string;
}

The docblock types matter. Magento's web API layer reads them to build the REST schema. A PHP native return type alone is not enough on older 2.4 patches; keep the @param and @return lines.

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/etc/db_schema.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<schema xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Setup/Declaration/Schema/etc/schema.xsd">
    <table name="maheshdave_order_export_status" resource="sales" engine="innodb" comment="ERP export state">
        <column xsi:type="varchar" name="increment_id" length="32" nullable="false" comment="Increment ID"/>
        <column xsi:type="varchar" name="state" length="16" nullable="false" comment="exported or failed"/>
        <column xsi:type="timestamp" name="updated_at" nullable="false" default="CURRENT_TIMESTAMP" on_update="true" comment="Updated at"/>
        <constraint xsi:type="primary" referenceId="PRIMARY">
            <column name="increment_id"/>
        </constraint>
    </table>
</schema>

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/Model/ExportStatus.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\OrderExport\Model;

use Magento\Framework\App\ResourceConnection;
use Magento\Framework\Exception\InputException;
use Magento\Framework\Exception\NoSuchEntityException;
use Magento\Sales\Api\OrderRepositoryInterface;
use Magento\Framework\Api\SearchCriteriaBuilder;
use MaheshDave\OrderExport\Api\ExportStatusInterface;

class ExportStatus implements ExportStatusInterface
{
    private const ALLOWED = ['exported', 'failed'];

    public function __construct(
        private readonly OrderRepositoryInterface $orderRepository,
        private readonly SearchCriteriaBuilder $searchCriteriaBuilder,
        private readonly ResourceConnection $resource
    ) {
    }

    public function setState(string $incrementId, string $state): string
    {
        if (!in_array($state, self::ALLOWED, true)) {
            throw new InputException(__('State must be exported or failed.'));
        }
        $criteria = $this->searchCriteriaBuilder
            ->addFilter('increment_id', $incrementId)
            ->setPageSize(1)
            ->create();
        $orders = $this->orderRepository->getList($criteria)->getItems();
        if ($orders === []) {
            throw new NoSuchEntityException(__('Order %1 does not exist.', $incrementId));
        }

        $connection = $this->resource->getConnection('sales');
        $connection->insertOnDuplicate(
            $this->resource->getTableName('maheshdave_order_export_status', 'sales'),
            ['increment_id' => $incrementId, 'state' => $state],
            ['state']
        );

        return $state;
    }
}

OrderRepositoryInterface::get() takes an entity id, not an increment id. Integrations send increment ids. getList with a filter is the supported lookup. There is no getByIncrementId on the repository interface; a helper with that name in some codebases is a local invention.

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/etc/di.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:ObjectManager/etc/config.xsd">
    <preference for="MaheshDave\OrderExport\Api\ExportStatusInterface" type="MaheshDave\OrderExport\Model\ExportStatus"/>
</config>

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/etc/webapi.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<routes xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:module:Magento_Webapi:etc/webapi.xsd">
    <route url="/V1/maheshdave/order-export/:incrementId" method="PUT">
        <service class="MaheshDave\OrderExport\Api\ExportStatusInterface" method="setState"/>
        <resources>
            <resource ref="MaheshDave_OrderExport::status"/>
        </resources>
    </route>
</routes>

The route parameter name has to match the PHP argument name, incrementId, not increment_id. The second argument comes from the body as {"state":"exported"}. Using anonymous as the resource would publish this to the internet. The ACL resource is declared in etc/acl.xml and granted to the integration in System > Integrations, not to a human admin role, unless a person is going to call it from the admin token.

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/etc/acl.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Acl/etc/acl.xsd">
    <acl>
        <resources>
            <resource id="Magento_Backend::admin">
                <resource id="MaheshDave_OrderExport::status" title="Update order export state" sortOrder="90"/>
            </resource>
        </resources>
    </acl>
</config>

The cron calls the interface

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/Cron/RetryFailed.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\OrderExport\Cron;

use MaheshDave\OrderExport\Api\ExportStatusInterface;

class RetryFailed
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly ExportStatusInterface $exportStatus
    ) {
    }

    public function execute(): void
    {
        $this->exportStatus->setState('000000123', 'failed');
    }
}

The hardcoded increment id is the shape of the call, not the selection logic. The selection belongs in a repository of your own; the point is that the cron has no curl back into /rest and no second writer. A cron that HTTP-calls the local REST API pays for auth, area emulation, and a network hop to change a row in the same database.

Check both callers

bin/magento setup:upgrade
bin/magento setup:di:compile
curl -s -X PUT "https://example.test/rest/V1/maheshdave/order-export/000000123" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"state":"exported"}'

A token whose role lacks MaheshDave_OrderExport::status gets 401 or 403. A bad state gets a 400 with the input exception message. Then:

SELECT increment_id, state FROM maheshdave_order_export_status WHERE increment_id = '000000123';

state is exported. Run the cron class from a command or from bin/magento cron:run after you point it at a real failed order, and the same row moves to failed with a newer updated_at. Two writers, one row, one method.

articles.title: An Admin Grid Whose Collection Is Not Loaded in the Browser
articles.excerpt: The export-status screen was a custom controller that loaded every row into a phtml. Filters were PHP array functions. The UI listing data source already does paging, filters, and ACL, if the collection name matches.
articles.content:
The first admin screen for export status selected every row in maheshdave_order_export_status, json-encoded it, and let Knockout filter. At a few hundred orders it felt instant. At the volume the ERP actually produces, the HTML request spent longer in PHP than the grid spent rendering, and a "filter by failed" still transferred the successes. Magento's listing component already sends filters and page size to mui/index/render. The work is to point that pipeline at the table, not to build a second one.

The name has to match in three places

The data provider name, the js_config provider string, and the collections item in di.xml are one identifier. A typo does not throw. The grid renders with an empty collection and a successful HTTP 200, which is why this survives QA on a fixture of zero rows.

        <item name="js_config" xsi:type="array">
            <item name="provider" xsi:type="string">maheshdave_export_status_listing.export_status_listing_data_source</item>
        </item>

        <spinner>export_status_columns</spinner>

            <dep>maheshdave_export_status_listing.export_status_listing_data_source</dep>

        <settings>
            <storageConfig>

            </storageConfig>
            <aclResource>MaheshDave_OrderExport::status</aclResource>
            <updateUrl path="mui/index/render"/>
        </settings>
        <dataProvider class="Magento\Framework\View\Element\UiComponent\DataProvider\DataProvider"
                      name="maheshdave_export_status_listing_data_source">
            <settings>
                <requestFieldName>increment_id</requestFieldName>
                <primaryFieldName>increment_id</primaryFieldName>
            </settings>
        </dataProvider>
    </dataSource>
    <columns name="export_status_columns">
        <selectionsColumn name="ids">
            <settings>
                <indexField>increment_id</indexField>
            </settings>
        </selectionsColumn>
        <column name="increment_id">
            <settings>
                <filter>text</filter>
                <label translate="true">Order</label>
            </settings>
        </column>
        <column name="state">
            <settings>
                <filter>text</filter>
