            </settings>
        </column>
    </columns>
</listing>

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/etc/di.xml (the collection argument, next to the preference from the service contract):

<type name="Magento\Framework\View\Element\UiComponent\DataProvider\CollectionFactory">
    <arguments>
        <argument name="collections" xsi:type="array">
            <item name="maheshdave_export_status_listing_data_source" xsi:type="string">MaheshDave\OrderExport\Model\ResourceModel\Status\Grid\Collection</item>
        </argument>
    </arguments>
</type>
<type name="MaheshDave\OrderExport\Model\ResourceModel\Status\Grid\Collection">
    <arguments>
        <argument name="mainTable" xsi:type="string">maheshdave_order_export_status</argument>
        <argument name="resourceModel" xsi:type="string">MaheshDave\OrderExport\Model\ResourceModel\Status</argument>
    </arguments>
</type>

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/Model/ResourceModel/Status.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\OrderExport\Model\ResourceModel;

use Magento\Framework\Model\ResourceModel\Db\AbstractDb;

class Status extends AbstractDb
{
    protected function _construct(): void
    {
        $this->_init('maheshdave_order_export_status', 'increment_id');
    }
}

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/Model/ResourceModel/Status/Grid/Collection.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\OrderExport\Model\ResourceModel\Status\Grid;

use Magento\Framework\View\Element\UiComponent\DataProvider\SearchResult;

class Collection extends SearchResult
{
}

SearchResult takes $mainTable and $resourceModel in its constructor. Setting them in di.xml keeps the collection class empty, which is what you want: grid behavior (filters, order, page size) is applied by Magento\Framework\View\Element\UiComponent\DataProvider\DataProvider onto this collection. A collection that calls load() inside _initSelect() defeats the paging, because the limit is applied too late or not at all if you already fetched.

The page that hosts it

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/Controller/Adminhtml/Status/Index.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\OrderExport\Controller\Adminhtml\Status;

use Magento\Backend\App\Action;
use Magento\Framework\App\Action\HttpGetActionInterface;
use Magento\Framework\View\Result\PageFactory;

class Index extends Action implements HttpGetActionInterface
{
    public const ADMIN_RESOURCE = 'MaheshDave_OrderExport::status';

    public function __construct(
        Action\Context $context,
        private readonly PageFactory $pageFactory
    ) {
        parent::__construct($context);
    }

    public function execute()
    {
        $page = $this->pageFactory->create();
        $page->setActiveMenu('MaheshDave_OrderExport::status');
        $page->getConfig()->getTitle()->prepend(__('Order export status'));

        return $page;
    }
}

articles.title: A Mass Action That Queues Work Instead of Timing Out
articles.excerpt: Retry-export on the order grid processed the selected rows inside the admin request. Two thousand rows blew the Fastly first-byte timeout. The request should publish ids and return.
articles.content:
"Retry export" on the status grid worked for the five orders QA selected. Operations selected the whole failed filter, about two thousand rows, and the admin tab spun until Fastly returned 503. The controller was calling the ERP inside the request. The browser, PHP-FPM, and Fastly all have timeouts shorter than that loop. The mass action's job is to record the selection and return a message. A consumer does the work.

The listing item

Inside maheshdave_export_status_listing.xml, as a sibling of columns:

<massaction name="listing_massaction">
    <action name="retry">
        <settings>
            <url path="maheshdave_export/status/retry"/>
            <type>retry</type>
            <label translate="true">Retry export</label>
            <actionType>basic</actionType>
        </settings>
    </action>
</massaction>

actionType>basic posts the selected ids. A confirmation modal is available and I use it when the action is destructive; a retry is not, and a modal on a retry trains people to click through it.

The controller publishes

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/Controller/Adminhtml/Status/Retry.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\OrderExport\Controller\Adminhtml\Status;

use Magento\Backend\App\Action;
use Magento\Backend\App\Action\Context;
use Magento\Framework\App\Action\HttpPostActionInterface;
use Magento\Framework\Controller\ResultFactory;
use Magento\Framework\MessageQueue\PublisherInterface;
use Magento\Ui\Component\MassAction\Filter;
use MaheshDave\OrderExport\Model\ResourceModel\Status\Grid\CollectionFactory;

class Retry extends Action implements HttpPostActionInterface
{
    public const ADMIN_RESOURCE = 'MaheshDave_OrderExport::status';
    public const TOPIC = 'maheshdave.order.export';

    public function __construct(
        Context $context,
        private readonly Filter $filter,
        private readonly CollectionFactory $collectionFactory,
        private readonly PublisherInterface $publisher
    ) {
        parent::__construct($context);
    }

    public function execute()
    {
        $collection = $this->filter->getCollection($this->collectionFactory->create());
        $count = 0;
        foreach ($collection->getAllIds() as $incrementId) {
            $this->publisher->publish(self::TOPIC, (string) $incrementId);
            $count++;
        }
        $this->messageManager->addSuccessMessage(__('%1 orders queued for export.', $count));

        return $this->resultFactory->create(ResultFactory::TYPE_REDIRECT)->setPath('maheshdave_export/status/index');
    }
}

Filter applies the selection, or the "select all across pages" excluded-id set, onto the collection. Reading $this->getRequest()->getParam('selected') yourself misses the excluded-ids case and retries the wrong page. getAllIds() returns the primary key. Publishing inside the loop is acceptable at a few thousand ids because each publish is an insert, not an HTTP call. If the selection can hit hundreds of thousands, write one bulk insert into queue_message or chunk through a single message that contains the filter, not the ids. I have not needed that for an operational retry.

The consumer is the one from the queue article, maheshdave.order.export, and it must tolerate a duplicate id. A merchant will click the action twice. insertOnDuplicate on the status row, and an ERP call keyed by increment id, make the second run a no-op. If the ERP call is not idempotent, do not queue it this way.

There is no CSRF token to add by hand. Admin POST actions go through Magento's form key via the UI component. A raw fetch you add later has to send form_key. This one does not.

What you should see

Select two failed rows, run Retry export. The page comes back in well under a second with "2 orders queued for export." Then:

SELECT topic_name, body FROM queue_message ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5;

Two bodies, the two increment ids, topic maheshdave.order.export. Start the consumer with --max-messages=2 and the ERP log (or the handler log) shows those two orders and nothing else. If the admin request itself logs ERP traffic, the controller is still doing the work and the queue is decoration.

articles.title: Website-Scoped Config That Reads the Default Value from Cron
articles.excerpt: A website-scoped ERP URL was correct in admin and wrong in cron, which has no store and therefore reads the default scope. Pass the website id into getValue.
articles.content:
The ERP base URL was set at the website scope for the EU site and left empty at default, on purpose, so the US site could not accidentally call the EU endpoint. Admin saves from the EU website worked. The cron export called the empty URL and logged "ERP base URL is not configured" for orders that belonged to the EU website. ScopeConfigInterface::getValue($path) with no scope uses the current scope. Cron, consumers, and bin/magento have no current store, so that call returns the default-scope value, which was empty.

Read the scope you mean

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/Model/ErpConfig.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\OrderExport\Model;

use Magento\Framework\App\Config\ScopeConfigInterface;
use Magento\Framework\Exception\LocalizedException;
use Magento\Store\Model\ScopeInterface;
use Magento\Store\Model\StoreManagerInterface;

class ErpConfig
{
    private const XML_PATH = 'maheshdave_erp/connection/base_url';

    public function __construct(
        private readonly ScopeConfigInterface $scopeConfig,
        private readonly StoreManagerInterface $storeManager
    ) {
    }

    public function getBaseUrlForStore(int $storeId): string
    {
        $websiteId = (int) $this->storeManager->getStore($storeId)->getWebsiteId();
        $url = trim((string) $this->scopeConfig->getValue(self::XML_PATH, ScopeInterface::SCOPE_WEBSITE, $websiteId));
        if ($url === '') {
            throw new LocalizedException(__('ERP base URL is not configured for website %1.', $websiteId));
        }

        return rtrim($url, '/');
    }
}

The third argument is the website id, not the store id, because the scope type is SCOPE_WEBSITE. Passing a store id there reads a different website's row, or none, and it does not throw. The order has a store_id. Resolve the website from that store. Do not take the website id from "the current website" inside a consumer; there isn't one.

A path that is configured at store-view scope has to be read with ScopeInterface::SCOPE_STORE and the store id. Website scope does not fall through per store view. If two store views in one website must call different endpoints, the field was created at the wrong scope and no amount of getValue flags will split it. Recreate it as store scope, or the values will keep colliding.

Where the store id comes from

The export message in this project is the order id. The consumer loads the order and then asks for config:

$order = $this->orderRepository->get((int) $orderId);
$baseUrl = $this->erpConfig->getBaseUrlForStore((int) $order->getStoreId());

That is the whole fix. Iterating $this->storeManager->getWebsites() is the other correct shape, and I use it when the job is not tied to an order: a catalog push that must run once per website. Running it once and reading default scope sends every website's products to whichever URL was saved at default, including websites you thought were isolated.

Prove the scope, not the value

bin/magento config:show maheshdave_erp/connection/base_url
bin/magento config:show --scope=websites --scope-code=eu maheshdave_erp/connection/base_url

The first command prints the default, often empty. The second prints the EU URL. After the consumer change, an EU order logs the EU host. A US order, with no website value and no default, throws the localized exception naming the website id, which is the outcome you configured. If both commands print the same URL, the value was saved at default and the website field in admin was never saved; the code is then doing what it should with the data it has.

articles.title: SearchCriteria Filters That Silently Return the Wrong Page
articles.excerpt: A REST order search returned page 1 of everything. The filter was built, then setPageSize created a new SearchCriteria and dropped it. addFilter on a builder that already has a group is the other half of the bug.
articles.content:
The integration asked for orders with status processing, page size 50. The response was 50 orders of every status. The repository was fine. The criteria object that arrived had no filter groups. The builder had been asked to create() twice, and create() clears the builder so the next caller does not inherit the previous request's filters. The second call, which only set the page size, was the object that got passed.

One create, at the end

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/Model/ProcessingOrders.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\OrderExport\Model;

use Magento\Framework\Api\SearchCriteriaBuilder;
use Magento\Framework\Api\SortOrderBuilder;
use Magento\Sales\Api\Data\OrderInterface;
use Magento\Sales\Api\OrderRepositoryInterface;

class ProcessingOrders
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly OrderRepositoryInterface $orderRepository,
        private readonly SearchCriteriaBuilder $searchCriteriaBuilder,
        private readonly SortOrderBuilder $sortOrderBuilder
    ) {
    }

    /**
     * @return OrderInterface[]
     */
    public function getPage(int $page): array
    {
        $sort = $this->sortOrderBuilder
            ->setField('entity_id')
            ->setDirection('ASC')
            ->create();
        $criteria = $this->searchCriteriaBuilder
            ->addFilter('status', 'processing')
            ->addFilter('store_id', 1)
            ->addSortOrder($sort)
            ->setPageSize(50)
            ->setCurrentPage($page)
            ->create();

        return $this->orderRepository->getList($criteria)->getItems();
    }
}

SortOrderBuilder::create() also resets. Build the sort, then the criteria, and do not call create() on the criteria builder to "peek". Builders are mutable and, in the default DI setup, not a fresh object per class if someone registered them as shared in a way that leaks; Magento creates them as shared unless you inject a proxy or a factory. create() clearing state is what makes a shared builder safe. If you stash the builder and add filters across requests in a long-running consumer, call create() or you will AND the new filters with the previous message's filters. I inject the builder and finish with one create() per message.

AND versus OR

Two addFilter calls on the same builder are ANDed. They become one filter group. Orders that are processing AND in store 1 is what the code above asks for. Orders that are processing OR pending need two groups:

$processing = $this->filterBuilder->setField('status')->setValue('processing')->create();
$pending = $this->filterBuilder->setField('status')->setValue('pending')->create();
$criteria = $this->searchCriteriaBuilder
    ->addFilters([$processing, $pending])
    ->setPageSize(50)
    ->create();

addFilters (plural) puts those filters in one group, and a group is OR. A later addFilter starts another group, which is AND across groups. Mixing them because the names look similar is how a "failed or exported, for this website" query drops the website. FilterBuilder is Magento\Framework\Api\FilterBuilder. It also resets on create().

getItems() is keyed by entity id. count($items) is the page, not the total. The total is getTotalCount() on the search result. Clients that stop when the page contains fewer than 50 rows are fine; clients that stop when count($items) === 0 are also fine. Clients that compare count($items) to getTotalCount() and expect them to match have confused the page with the whole result.

Look at the criteria, not the JSON

Log $criteria->getFilterGroups() before getList while reproducing. An empty array means the builder was reset or the filters were never added. A single group with two filters is the AND. Two groups means an OR plus something else. Then call the REST method the integration uses and compare total_count with:

SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sales_order WHERE status = 'processing' AND store_id = 1;

Those numbers match when the criteria survived. If the SQL count is 40 and total_count is the size of sales_order, the filter group is empty and the page size is the only part that arrived.

articles.title: Category Pages That Stay Stale After a Catalog Reindex
articles.excerpt: After a catalog reindex, product pages refreshed and category pages kept yesterday's product list. The indexer purged product tags. Category pages are stored under cat_c.
articles.content:
Product pages updated within a minute of a price import. Category pages, which list those products, still showed the old price and the old position until someone purged the whole site. The import and the indexer were doing what they were written to do: they registered product cache tags. A category page in full-page cache is tagged with the category, cat_c_{id}, and Fastly keeps serving it until that tag is purged. Soft-purging a product tag does not select the category object.

Magento\Catalog\Model\Category::CACHE_TAG is cat_c. Magento\Catalog\Model\Product::CACHE_TAG is cat_p. The page-cache identifier is {tag}_{id}. Fastly's Commerce module purges the tags Magento hands it through the cache-invalidation flow. If the tag was never registered, there is nothing to purge, and a "soft purge" setting is not the thing that is wrong.

Register the category ids the reindex actually changed

Plug in after the category-product indexer processes a list of product ids, resolve the categories those products are in, and register those category tags. Then dispatch clean_cache_by_tags, which is the event the cache-invalidation layer listens on.

app/code/MaheshDave/CatalogCache/Plugin/PurgeCategoriesAfterProductReindex.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\CatalogCache\Plugin;

use Magento\Catalog\Model\Category;
use Magento\Catalog\Model\Indexer\Product\Category as CategoryProductIndexer;
use Magento\Framework\Event\ManagerInterface;
use Magento\Framework\Indexer\CacheContext;
use Magento\Framework\App\ResourceConnection;

class PurgeCategoriesAfterProductReindex
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly CacheContext $cacheContext,
        private readonly ManagerInterface $eventManager,
        private readonly ResourceConnection $resource
    ) {
    }

    /**
     * @param int[] $ids
     */
    public function afterExecuteList(CategoryProductIndexer $subject, $result, array $ids)
    {
        $this->purgeForProducts($ids);

        return $result;
    }

    /**
     * @param int[] $productIds
     */
    private function purgeForProducts(array $productIds): void
    {
        $productIds = array_values(array_unique(array_map('intval', $productIds)));
        if ($productIds === []) {
            return;
        }
        $connection = $this->resource->getConnection();
        $select = $connection->select()
            ->from($this->resource->getTableName('catalog_category_product'), ['category_id'])
            ->where('product_id IN (?)', $productIds)
            ->distinct(true);
        $categoryIds = array_map('intval', $connection->fetchCol($select));
        if ($categoryIds === []) {
            return;
        }
        $this->cacheContext->registerEntities(Category::CACHE_TAG, $categoryIds);
        $this->eventManager->dispatch('clean_cache_by_tags', ['object' => $this->cacheContext]);
    }
}

app/code/MaheshDave/CatalogCache/etc/di.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:ObjectManager/etc/config.xsd">
    <type name="Magento\Catalog\Model\Indexer\Product\Category">
        <plugin name="maheshdave_purge_categories" type="MaheshDave\CatalogCache\Plugin\PurgeCategoriesAfterProductReindex"/>
    </type>
</config>

This plugin runs for the partial list. A full executeFull on a large catalog would resolve every category and purge almost the whole FPC, which is the flush you were trying not to do, only slower. I do not attach it to executeFull. A nightly full reindex can purge cat_c once, deliberately, in a maintenance window. Schedule mode ("Update by Schedule") calls the list path with the changelog ids, which is the path this covers.

Anchor categories and categories that include the product through a rule rather than catalog_category_product are not in that select. If the stale page is a visual-merchandiser category, the row may live in the index table catalog_category_product_index instead. Read the store-scoped index table for that case, and expect one row per store, so distinct still matters.

Check the tag, then the page

bin/magento setup:di:compile
bin/magento indexer:reindex catalog_category_product

In developer mode the category response sends X-Magento-Tags. Confirm cat_c_4 (or whichever id) is on the category URL before you blame Fastly. Change a product in that category, run bin/magento cron:run --group=index if the indexer is on schedule, and request the category again. The first request after the purge is a miss and shows the new price. If the tags header contains only cat_p_* and store tags, the category block is not adding its identity, and purging cat_c will never select that object. That is a block identity problem, not an indexer problem.

articles.title: Bypassing Fastly for One Query Parameter Only
articles.excerpt: A preview query parameter was added to the cache hash, so every campaign link became its own object. Pass on that one parameter in vcl_recv and strip it from the cache key instead.
articles.content:
Marketing appended utm_source to every category URL. Fastly's hit rate on those categories collapsed, because the query string was part of the cache key and each combination was a new object. Someone then added a VCL pass for any request with a query string. Hit rate came back for clean URLs and category filters, which are also a query string, started hitting origin on every request. The requirement was narrower than either change: a preview=1 flag used by merchandisers must not be cached, and every other parameter must not multiply objects.

Two different operations

Passing and stripping solve different problems. return(pass) in vcl_recv sends this request to origin and does not store the response. That is correct for preview, because the preview response must not be saved and later served to a shopper. A tracking parameter should be stored, but under a key that does not include it. That is req.url rewritten before the hash, or set req.http.Fastly-Purge is unrelated; the usual Commerce approach is to remove the parameter from the URL that Fastly hashes while leaving the original available to origin if origin needs it. For UTM, origin does not need it to render a category. Remove it from the URL used as the key.

This is a custom snippet in the Fastly configuration for the Commerce service, type recv, priority after the stock Magento snippets so you do not fight their admin and checkout passes. Upload VCL after saving. A snippet that exists only in the Magento admin and was never uploaded is not running.

if (req.url.qs ~ "(^|&)preview=") {
    set req.http.X-Magento-Preview = "1";
    return (pass);
}

if (req.url ~ "\?") {
    set req.url = querystring.filter(req.url, "utm_source");
    set req.url = querystring.filter(req.url, "utm_medium");
    set req.url = querystring.filter(req.url, "utm_campaign");
    set req.url = querystring.filter(req.url, "utm_content");
    set req.url = querystring.filter(req.url, "utm_term");
}

querystring.filter is a Fastly VCL function, not part of the Varnish this site runs locally. A snippet that works in a local Varnish 6 file will fail validation on Fastly if it calls that function the other way around, and a failed validation does not activate, so the previous version stays live. That is the safe failure. Validate before activate. The manual Fastly CLI article in this set is the procedure I use when a snippet has to come back out.

return(pass) stops processing of vcl_recv. The filter block must stay below the preview check or preview URLs get stripped and then cached. Do not match req.url.qs ~ ".". That is the "any query string" pass that broke layered navigation.

What a hit looks like after this

Request the category with and without utm_source=newsletter. Both should return the same X-Cache HIT and the same Age growing together. If the ages differ, the parameter is still in the key: the snippet is not on the active VCL version. Request ?preview=1 twice. Both should be PASS or MISS, never a HIT that grows Age. If preview hits, the condition did not run, often because the parameter was added as ?x=1&preview without a value and the regex expected preview=. The pattern above requires the equals sign. Merchandisers were copying a link without it, so I also match (^|&)preview($|&) when the flag is boolean. I keep that second condition in the same if, not in a later snippet, so there is one place that decides to pass.

articles.title: A Custom Block Fastly Never Purges
articles.excerpt: A CMS-driven banner block stayed on the category page for as long as the page was cached. The block never implemented IdentityInterface, so a save had no tag to purge.
articles.content:
The category page cached correctly. A merchandiser updated the promo row that feeds the banner on that page, flushed nothing, and waited. The banner did not change until the page TTL expired. The block rendered the promo during the miss and then became anonymous bytes inside the page. Full-page cache purges by tag. A block that does not declare identities adds no tag, so a save of the promo has nothing to purge.

Identities on the block

app/code/MaheshDave/PromoBanner/Block/Banner.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\PromoBanner\Block;

use Magento\Framework\DataObject\IdentityInterface;
use Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template;
use MaheshDave\PromoBanner\Model\Promo;
use MaheshDave\PromoBanner\Model\PromoRepository;

class Banner extends Template implements IdentityInterface
{
    public function __construct(
        Template\Context $context,
        private readonly PromoRepository $promoRepository,
        array $data = []
    ) {
        parent::__construct($context, $data);
    }

    public function getPromo(): ?Promo
    {
        $id = (int) $this->getData('promo_id');

        return $id > 0 ? $this->promoRepository->get($id) : null;
    }

    public function getIdentities(): array
    {
        $promo = $this->getPromo();

        return $promo === null ? [] : $promo->getIdentities();
    }
}

The model owns the tag format so the block and the purge on save cannot drift.

app/code/MaheshDave/PromoBanner/Model/Promo.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\PromoBanner\Model;

use Magento\Framework\DataObject\IdentityInterface;
use Magento\Framework\Model\AbstractModel;

class Promo extends AbstractModel implements IdentityInterface
{
    public const CACHE_TAG = 'maheshdave_promo';

    public function getIdentities(): array
    {
        return [self::CACHE_TAG . '_' . $this->getId()];
    }
}

On save, the abstract model already asks for identities when the model implements the interface, and the page-cache layer collects them. Calling clean_cache_by_tags yourself on top of that double-purges and is how a busy admin save turns into a stampede. I only dispatch that event when the write path does not go through the model, which is the same situation as a bulk SQL update.

The block has to actually be rendered inside the cached page. A block created in a controller and echoed, or filled via AJAX after load, is not part of the FPC document and its identities are never recorded. Layout XML is what puts it in the hole punch list Magento walks:

<referenceContainer name="content">
    <block class="MaheshDave\PromoBanner\Block\Banner" name="maheshdave.promo.banner" template="MaheshDave_PromoBanner::banner.phtml">
        <arguments>
            <argument name="promo_id" xsi:type="string">14</argument>
        </arguments>
    </block>
</referenceContainer>

cacheable="false" on this block does purge nothing faster. It disables caching for the entire page, which hides the bug by never storing the page. Leave it cacheable and give it a tag.

See the tag, change the row, see it go

With developer mode on, the category response includes X-Magento-Tags containing maheshdave_promo_14. If the tag is absent, the block was not rendered on that request (wrong handle, empty promo_id). Save the promo in admin. The next category request is a miss and the banner text matches the save. A hit with the old text and the tag present means the save path did not purge: the admin form is writing SQL without the model. Move that write onto the repository, or register Promo::CACHE_TAG with the saved id and dispatch clean_cache_by_tags there.

articles.seo_description: Implement IdentityInterface on a Magento block so Fastly and FPC purge it when the underlying record changes, instead of waiting out the TTL.

articles.title: The Block That Turns Off Full-Page Cache for the Whole Page
articles.excerpt: One block with cacheable="false" made every category page a Fastly pass. The block showed the customer's first name. That data belongs in a customer-data section, and the page stays cacheable.
articles.content:
Category TTFB went from tens of milliseconds at Fastly to a full origin render, on every request, after a "small" header change that printed the logged-in customer's first name. The template was fine. The layout node had cacheable="false". Magento's rule is not "this block is private". It is "if any block in the layout is not cacheable, the page is not cacheable". Fastly then has nothing worth storing, because origin sends the response as uncacheable.

Find it before rewriting the page. From the Magento root, the layouts you own are the ones to change; core uses the flag for checkout and customer account on purpose.

rg -n 'cacheable="false"' app/code app/design --glob '*.xml'

The header block in this case existed only to greet the customer. Everyone else, including guests, paid for an uncached page so that one string could be personal. Customer-specific fragments in Magento are loaded in the browser from /customer/section/load after the cached HTML is served. The page stays public. The section payload is per session.

The section

app/code/MaheshDave/Greeting/etc/frontend/sections.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:module:Magento_Customer:etc/sections.xsd">
    <action name="customer/account/loginPost">
        <section name="maheshdave-greeting"/>
    </action>
    <action name="customer/account/logout">
        <section name="maheshdave-greeting"/>
    </action>
</config>

Those actions invalidate the section so the next page load refetches it. A section that is never invalidated shows the previous customer's name after a logout on a page that was sitting in the browser. Login and logout are the minimum.

app/code/MaheshDave/Greeting/CustomerData/Greeting.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\Greeting\CustomerData;

use Magento\Customer\CustomerData\SectionSourceInterface;
use Magento\Customer\Helper\Session\CurrentCustomer;

class Greeting implements SectionSourceInterface
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly CurrentCustomer $currentCustomer
    ) {
    }

    public function getSectionData(): array
    {
        if (!$this->currentCustomer->getCustomerId()) {
            return ['firstname' => ''];
        }

        return ['firstname' => (string) $this->currentCustomer->getCustomer()->getFirstname()];
    }
}

app/code/MaheshDave/Greeting/etc/frontend/di.xml

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:ObjectManager/etc/config.xsd">
    <type name="Magento\Customer\CustomerData\SectionPoolInterface">
        <arguments>
            <argument name="sectionSourceMap" xsi:type="array">
                <item name="maheshdave-greeting" xsi:type="string">MaheshDave\Greeting\CustomerData\Greeting</item>
            </argument>
        </arguments>
    </type>
</config>

app/code/MaheshDave/Greeting/view/frontend/templates/greeting.phtml

<span class="maheshdave-greeting" data-bind="scope: 'maheshdave-greeting'">
    <!-- ko if: greeting().firstname -->
    <span data-bind="text: greeting().firstname"></span>
    <!-- /ko -->
</span>
<script type="text/x-magento-init">
{
    "*": {
        "Magento_Ui/js/core/app": {
            "components": {
                "maheshdave-greeting": {
                    "component": "Magento_Customer/js/view/customer"
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
</script>

The template above is the shape, and the component name has to be a UI component that reads the section. The stock customer component reads the customer section, not yours. Use a small component that returns the section:

app/code/MaheshDave/Greeting/view/frontend/web/js/greeting.js

define(['uiComponent', 'Magento_Customer/js/customer-data'], function (Component, customerData) {
    'use strict';

    return Component.extend({
        initialize: function () {
            this._super();
            this.greeting = customerData.get('maheshdave-greeting');
            return this;
        }
    });
});

Point the Magento_Ui/js/core/app component at MaheshDave_Greeting/js/greeting. Remove cacheable="false" from the block. The phtml no longer prints the name in PHP, so the cached HTML is the same for every visitor and the name appears after customer-data loads.

Confirm the page is cacheable again

Fetch a category URL twice and read X-Magento-Cache-Debug in developer mode, or Fastly X-Cache. The second response is a HIT. View source on that HIT and confirm the first name is not in the HTML. It should appear only after the section request to /customer/section/load?sections=maheshdave-greeting. If the name is in the HTML of a HIT, the old block is still rendering it and you have two sources. If the page is still a pass, another cacheable="false" remains in the handle. The rg result is the list, not a suggestion.

articles.title: Naming Cron and Consumer Transactions in New Relic
articles.excerpt: Cron and queue consumers showed up in New Relic as one transaction named index.php, so a slow export was invisible next to storefront traffic. Name the transaction after the job.
articles.content:
The New Relic overview for this service was dominated by WebTransaction/Action/index and a lump of CLI time called something like OtherTransaction/php/bin/magento. A 40-second order export ran every five minutes inside cron and never appeared as its own transaction. Apdex and error rate were storefront numbers. The export could fail all night and the only signal was a queue depth someone happened to query.

The PHP agent names web transactions from the framework when the framework calls the agent. Magento's web front does that. bin/magento cron:run does not name each job, and a consumer process lives until maxMessages, so one process name covers a hundred different messages. Set the name at the start of the job. The functions are newrelic_name_transaction and newrelic_add_custom_parameter, provided by the New Relic PHP extension. Guard them with function_exists so local DDEV, which has no agent, does not throw.

app/code/MaheshDave/DevTools/Model/NewRelic/Transaction.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\DevTools\Model\NewRelic;

class Transaction
{
    public function name(string $name, array $parameters = []): void
    {
        if (function_exists('newrelic_name_transaction')) {
            newrelic_name_transaction($name);
        }
        if (!function_exists('newrelic_add_custom_parameter')) {
            return;
        }
        foreach ($parameters as $key => $value) {
            if (is_scalar($value)) {
                newrelic_add_custom_parameter((string) $key, $value);
            }
        }
    }
}

Call it before the work, not after. A name set at the end still helps the next segment, but the time already recorded sits on the previous name.

$this->transaction->name('cron/maheshdave_order_export', ['website_id' => $websiteId]);

Inside a consumer, name it once per message and include the topic, not the order id. An order id as a transaction name creates one unique name per order and New Relic drops them as cardinality noise. The order id belongs in a custom parameter only if you accept that it is high cardinality; I put the increment id in the log line and keep the parameter set to the store id.

$this->transaction->name('consumer/maheshdave.order.export', ['store_id' => (int) $order->getStoreId()]);

The module is MaheshDave_DevTools because this is diagnostic instrumentation, not order-export business logic. The export module depends on DevTools or, if you refuse that dependency, duplicate the ten-line class. I depend on it. A consumer that catches exceptions and does not rethrow looks successful to the agent. Call newrelic_notice_error with the exception in that catch, or the error rate stays flat while the log fills up. That function is also part of the agent and needs the same function_exists check.

What changes in the UI

After one cron cycle with the agent installed, Transaction shows cron/maheshdave_order_export with a duration you can compare to the schedule. The consumer name appears as its own row instead of being folded into bin/magento. Filter request.uri or transaction name LIKE 'cron/%' and the storefront disappears. If nothing new shows up, the CLI binary is a different PHP than the one with the extension: php -m | grep newrelic using the same binary cron uses. A web SAPI with the extension and a CLI SAPI without it is the usual split.

articles.seo_description: Magento cron and consumers report as a generic PHP transaction. Name them with the New Relic PHP agent so a slow job is visible.

articles.title: NRQL for Checkout Latency by Store
articles.excerpt: Average checkout duration hid a store that had slowed down after a tax change. Facet the New Relic transaction by store and by the checkout action, and alert on the facet, not the average.
articles.content:
Checkout "looked fine" in New Relic because the US store is most of the traffic and it was fine. The EU store's payment step had picked up two extra tax requests and moved from about 1.2s to about 4s. The un-faceted average moved by a tenth of a second, inside the noise. The alert on average duration did not fire. Facet by the store custom parameter from the start, or this shape of regression does not exist in the dashboard you are watching.

The parameter has to be on the transaction before NRQL can facet it. In the checkout module I add it from an observer on controller_action_predispatch_checkout, using the same MaheshDave\DevTools\Model\NewRelic\Transaction helper, with store_id and store_code. Naming the transaction is Magento's job for a front controller; the parameter is the part Magento does not set. I use the store code in NRQL because an id means nothing in an incident channel.

Queries I actually keep

Duration of the payment place-order action, per store, last two hours:

SELECT average(duration), percentile(duration, 95)
FROM Transaction
WHERE appName = 'magento-prod'
  AND name = 'WebTransaction/Action/checkout_onepage_savePayment'
FACET store_code
SINCE 2 hours ago

The transaction name on your account may be the route Magento reported, not this string. Open one slow trace and copy the name. Do not guess it in the alert and then wonder why the alert never matches. percentile is the number I alert on. The average stays on the chart so a single stalled request is visible as a gap between the two.

Errors that are not storefront 200s with an empty message:

SELECT count(*)
FROM TransactionError
WHERE appName = 'magento-prod'
  AND request.uri LIKE '%/checkout/%'
FACET store_code, error.message
SINCE 1 hour ago

A facet with thousands of distinct messages is an exception that includes the order id in the message. Fix the message. The facet is unusable until you do, and New Relic will cap it.

Compare this week to last week for one store without trusting memory:

SELECT average(duration)
FROM Transaction
WHERE appName = 'magento-prod'
  AND name = 'WebTransaction/Action/checkout_onepage_savePayment'
  AND store_code = 'eu'
SINCE 7 days ago
COMPARE WITH 1 week ago
TIMESERIES 1 day

This is the chart that would have shown the tax change on the day it deployed. I put a deployment marker in New Relic from the pipeline (newrelic entity deployment or the marker API the account already uses) so the timeseries has a vertical line. A line without a marker is a guess about which release did it.

The alert

Alert when percentile(duration, 95) > 3 for at least 5 minutes, faceted by store_code, on that transaction name. A single global threshold of 3 seconds never fires if the US store is 0.8s and is 80% of samples, even while EU is at 4s. Facet alerts create one incident per store. That is what you want. Mute it for the store you are load-testing, not for the application.

If store_code is null on checkout transactions, the observer did not run for that controller. GraphQL checkout (placeOrder mutation) is a different transaction name entirely and will not appear in the web-controller query. Add a second alert on the GraphQL transaction once you have named or parameterized it. One dashboard that only knows about checkout_onepage_savePayment goes green the day you move checkout to GraphQL, which is the worst possible time for it to go green.

articles.seo_title: NRQL for Checkout Latency by Store
articles.seo_description: Break Magento checkout transaction time out by store with NRQL, instead of trusting an average that hides one slow website.

articles.title: From a New Relic Slow Query to an Index You Can Ship
articles.excerpt: New Relic showed a 2-second SELECT on the export-status table during the admin grid. EXPLAIN said it was scanning the whole table. The index belongs in db_schema.xml, not in a migration someone runs by hand.
articles.content:
The export-status grid filtered by state = 'failed' and ordered by updated_at. New Relic's slow SQL list showed that select at about two seconds once the table passed a few hundred thousand rows. The database tab is not proof. It is a candidate. I copy the SQL, run EXPLAIN on a replica, and only then add an index. An index for a query that is slow because it returns 100,000 rows does nothing but slow down the writes.

EXPLAIN SELECT increment_id, state, updated_at
FROM maheshdave_order_export_status
WHERE state = 'failed'
ORDER BY updated_at DESC
LIMIT 20;

type ALL and rows equal to the table size means there is no usable index. Using filesort in Extra on top of that is the sort of the whole filtered set. The index that matches this plan is (state, updated_at). state alone filters but still filesorts. updated_at alone does not satisfy the WHERE, so MySQL ignores it for this query.

Declare it

An ALTER TABLE on production, or an index added in phpMyAdmin, disappears the next time someone rebuilds an environment from db_schema.xml, and declarative schema may also drop it if the whitelist says the module owns the table and the XML does not mention the index. Put the index in the schema and regenerate the whitelist.

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/etc/db_schema.xml gains, inside the existing table node:

<index referenceId="MAHESHDAVE_ORDER_EXPORT_STATUS_STATE_UPDATED" indexType="btree">
    <column name="state"/>
    <column name="updated_at"/>
</index>
bin/magento setup:db-declaration:generate-whitelist --module-name=MaheshDave_OrderExport
bin/magento setup:upgrade --dry-run=1

The dry-run log should show an ADD INDEX and nothing else. If it shows column drops, stop. The whitelist or the XML does not match the table that is live. On a table this size the alter is the risk: it can lock writes for the duration on MySQL versions and settings that do not allow ALGORITHM=INPLACE for that index. Read the statement in the dry-run log. Run it in the window you would run any other alter, not as a side effect of a code deploy you described as "no schema change".

After setup:upgrade:

EXPLAIN SELECT increment_id, state, updated_at
FROM maheshdave_order_export_status
WHERE state = 'failed'
ORDER BY updated_at DESC
LIMIT 20;

Do not add a second index on updated_at alone "just in case". The grid's WHERE is state first. A leftover single-column index makes the optimizer's choice depend on statistics, and the plan you explained today is not the plan you get after the next analyze. One composite index that matches the query is the change.

type is ref and key is the new index. rows is the number of failed orders, not the table. Reload the admin grid and the New Relic slow-SQL row for this statement should fall off within the agent's harvest, not next week. If EXPLAIN still says ALL, the query in the grid is not the query you think: the data provider may be adding a join or a different order. Copy it from var/debug/db.log with the query log on, and explain that text. Index the SQL the application runs.

articles.seo_description: Take a slow Magento query from New Relic, confirm it with EXPLAIN, and add the index in db_schema.xml so the next deploy keeps it.

articles.title: Ack an Order Event in App Builder Before the Work Starts
articles.excerpt: An App Builder action that called the ERP before returning caused Adobe I/O to retry the order event, and the ERP created two documents. Acknowledge first, then do the work in a second invocation.
articles.content:
The order-placed event was subscribed to a Runtime action that loaded the order from Commerce, posted it to the ERP, and then returned 200. The ERP call took longer than the event delivery window often enough that I/O delivered the same event again. The action had no memory of the first attempt, so the ERP created a second document. The fix is not a longer timeout. The action that receives the event has to finish quickly and durably record the event id, and a second action does the ERP call.

This is the shape I deploy. The event envelope fields below are the CloudEvents fields Adobe I/O Events delivers to a Runtime web action (specversion, id, type, data). Confirm the Commerce payload inside data against the event you subscribed to; order increment id placement in that object has moved between event versions, so the code reads it defensively and records the raw event id either way.

actions/order-placed/index.js

const { Core } = require('@adobe/aio-sdk')

async function main (params) {
  const logger = Core.Logger('order-placed', { level: params.LOG_LEVEL || 'info' })
  const event = readEvent(params)
  if (!event.id) {
    logger.error('event id missing')
    return { statusCode: 200, body: { status: 'ignored' } }
  }

  const state = await Core.State.init()
  const seen = await state.get(`order-event:${event.id}`)
  if (seen) {
    return { statusCode: 200, body: { status: 'duplicate' } }
  }
  await state.put(`order-event:${event.id}`, JSON.stringify({ type: event.type, at: Date.now() }), { ttl: 604800 })

  // The heavy call belongs in a separate action, invoked after this returns.
  logger.info(JSON.stringify({ id: event.id, type: event.type, order: event.order }))
  return { statusCode: 200, body: { status: 'accepted', id: event.id } }
}

function readEvent (params) {
  let body = params
  if (typeof params.__ow_body === 'string' && params.__ow_body !== '') {
    try {
      body = JSON.parse(params.__ow_body)
    } catch (e) {
      body = {}
    }
  }
  const data = body.data || {}
  return {
    id: body.id || '',
    type: body.type || '',
    order: data.increment_id || data.order_increment_id || ''
  }
}

exports.main = main

Returning 200 for a malformed event is deliberate. A 500 makes I/O retry a body you will never parse. A duplicate event id returns 200 without writing a second state record. State TTL is seven days; an event redelivered after that can be processed again, which is why the ERP call itself also has to be idempotent on the order increment id. State is the fast dedupe, not the only one.

I do not call the ERP in this function. The follow-up action is a second Runtime action triggered by a queue or by OpenWhisk activation you fire only after state.put succeeds. If state.put throws, return 500 so the event is retried; you have not recorded it, and you have not called the ERP. That is the only 500 in this file.

The Commerce credential for the follow-up action comes from action parameters (params.COMMERCE_BASE_URL, an IMS token), set as secrets in the App Builder workspace, not written into index.js. Logging the whole params object logs those secrets into activation logs. Log the event id and the order number.

How I check it

Publish a test event twice with the same id. The first activation log says accepted. The second says duplicate. aio runtime activation list shows both under a second. If the first activation is multiple seconds and the ERP dashboard shows a document, the ERP call is still in this action and the state write is not protecting you from a timeout retry that happens before state.put.

articles.seo_title: Ack Commerce Events Before the Work
articles.seo_description: Return from an App Builder Runtime action before calling the ERP. Event retries otherwise create duplicate documents.

articles.title: A Webhook Receiver That Survives Retries
articles.excerpt: The ERP retried shipment notifications whenever Magento answered slowly, and each retry created another shipment. Store the event id first, create the shipment second, and return the same result on a replay.
articles.content:
The ERP sent a shipment notification, Magento created the shipment, and the connection dropped before the 200 reached the ERP. The ERP retried. Magento created a second shipment for the same items and the order went to a state the warehouse could not reconcile. Timeouts and retries are the normal behavior of the caller. The receiver that is not idempotent is the defect.

The header I require is X-Event-Id, which the ERP already generates, and X-Signature, an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body using a shared secret stored in Magento config (encrypted, not in the repo). I reject the request before any write if either is missing or the signature does not match.

app/code/MaheshDave/ErpWebhook/Controller/Shipment/Notify.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\ErpWebhook\Controller\Shipment;

use Magento\Framework\App\Action\HttpPostActionInterface;
use Magento\Framework\App\CsrfAwareActionInterface;
use Magento\Framework\App\Request\InvalidRequestException;
use Magento\Framework\App\RequestInterface;
use Magento\Framework\Controller\Result\JsonFactory;
use MaheshDave\ErpWebhook\Model\ShipmentNotifier;

class Notify implements HttpPostActionInterface, CsrfAwareActionInterface
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly RequestInterface $request,
        private readonly JsonFactory $jsonFactory,
        private readonly ShipmentNotifier $notifier
    ) {
    }

    public function execute()
    {
        $result = $this->jsonFactory->create();
        try {
            $outcome = $this->notifier->handle(
                (string) $this->request->getContent(),
                (string) $this->request->getHeader('X-Event-Id'),
                (string) $this->request->getHeader('X-Signature')
            );
        } catch (\Magento\Framework\Exception\LocalizedException $e) {
            return $result->setHttpResponseCode(400)->setData(['error' => $e->getMessage()]);
        }

        return $result->setData($outcome);
    }

    public function createCsrfValidationException(RequestInterface $request): ?InvalidRequestException
    {
        return null;
    }

    public function validateForCsrf(RequestInterface $request): ?bool
    {
        return true;
    }
}

CSRF validation has to be skipped because the caller is not a browser with a form key. That is safe only because the signature check is mandatory. A controller that returns true from validateForCsrf and does not verify a signature is an open endpoint.

app/code/MaheshDave/ErpWebhook/Model/ShipmentNotifier.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\ErpWebhook\Model;

use Magento\Framework\App\Config\ScopeConfigInterface;
use Magento\Framework\App\ResourceConnection;
use Magento\Framework\Exception\LocalizedException;

class ShipmentNotifier
{
    private const TABLE = 'maheshdave_webhook_event';

    public function __construct(
        private readonly ScopeConfigInterface $scopeConfig,
        private readonly ResourceConnection $resource
    ) {
    }

    public function handle(string $rawBody, string $eventId, string $signature): array
    {
        if ($eventId === '' || $signature === '') {
            throw new LocalizedException(__('Event id and signature are required.'));
        }
        $secret = (string) $this->scopeConfig->getValue('maheshdave_erp/webhook/secret');
        $expected = hash_hmac('sha256', $rawBody, $secret);
        if (!hash_equals($expected, $signature)) {
            throw new LocalizedException(__('Signature does not match.'));
        }

        $connection = $this->resource->getConnection();
        $table = $this->resource->getTableName(self::TABLE);
        $inserted = $connection->insertOnDuplicate($table, [
            'event_id' => $eventId,
            'payload' => $rawBody,
        ], []);
        if ($inserted === 0) {
            return ['status' => 'duplicate', 'event_id' => $eventId];
        }

        return ['status' => 'accepted', 'event_id' => $eventId];
    }
}

insertOnDuplicate with an empty update list still reports a duplicate key as an affected-row count of 0 when the row exists and no column changes. I rely on a primary key on event_id. Insert the event row before creating the shipment. If shipment creation throws, leave the row and return 500 only if you delete the row in the same failure path; otherwise a retry hits the duplicate branch and the shipment is never created. The version I run stores status on the event row (accepted, then processed) and the duplicate branch returns the stored result after retrying the shipment step when status is still accepted. The snippet above is the gate. The shipment call, using Magento\Sales\Api\ShipOrderInterface, sits between the insert and the response, and a unique key on the shipment's ERP document number inside that call is the second lock.

db_schema.xml for maheshdave_webhook_event has event_id varchar 64 as the primary key, payload as mediumtext, and received_at timestamp default current. Route the controller at erpwebhook/shipment/notify in etc/frontend/routes.xml only if you want a storefront URL; I put it on webapi.xml as an anonymous route when the signature is the authorization, and I do not also leave a frontend route up.

Replay the same body

BODY='{"order":"000000123","items":[{"sku":"24-MB01","qty":1}]}'
SIG=$(php -r "echo hash_hmac('sha256', getenv('BODY') ?: '', getenv('SECRET'));")
curl -s -X POST "https://example.test/rest/V1/maheshdave/shipment-notify" \
  -H "X-Event-Id: evt-1001" -H "X-Signature: $SIG" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "$BODY"

Run it twice. The first body is accepted. The second is duplicate. sales_shipment has one new row, not two. Change one byte of the body without changing the signature and the response is the signature error with no insert.

articles.seo_title: A Webhook That Survives Retries
articles.seo_description: Verify the HMAC, store the webhook id, and make Magento shipment creation idempotent so ERP retries do not ship the order twice.

articles.title: An Outbox So Placed Orders Reach the ERP After a Crash
articles.excerpt: A plugin called the ERP during place order. The ERP timed out, the customer retried, and some orders never left Magento because the process died after commit. Write an outbox row in the same transaction as the order and publish after.
articles.content:
Calling the ERP from checkout_submit_all_after couples the customer's request to a system you do not control. When the ERP is slow, checkout is slow. When the PHP process is killed after the order commits and before the HTTP call returns, the order exists and the ERP never hears about it. There is no row you can query to find those. An outbox row written next to the order is the list of work, and it survives the crash because it commits with the order.

Magento does not enlist your HTTP call in the database transaction. It will enlist an insert you run on the same connection before the order save completes, if you do the insert in sales_order_save_after while the transaction is still open. Observers on that event run inside the save. A queue publish does not. I insert the outbox row in the observer and publish only after a successful response is not required; a cron publishes rows that are still pending, so a publish that never happened is recovered.

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/Observer/WriteOutbox.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\OrderExport\Observer;

use Magento\Framework\App\ResourceConnection;
use Magento\Framework\Event\Observer;
use Magento\Framework\Event\ObserverInterface;
use Magento\Sales\Api\Data\OrderInterface;

class WriteOutbox implements ObserverInterface
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly ResourceConnection $resource
    ) {
    }

    public function execute(Observer $observer): void
    {
        $order = $observer->getEvent()->getOrder();
        if (!$order instanceof OrderInterface || !$order->getEntityId()) {
            return;
        }
        if (!$order->getOrigData('entity_id')) {
            $this->resource->getConnection()->insertOnDuplicate(
                $this->resource->getTableName('maheshdave_order_outbox'),
                ['order_id' => (int) $order->getEntityId(), 'status' => 'pending'],
                []
            );
        }
    }
}

getOrigData('entity_id') is empty on the insert and populated on later saves, so a status change does not enqueue the order again. events.xml listens to sales_order_save_after. The table's primary key is order_id, which makes a double-fired event harmless.

app/code/MaheshDave/OrderExport/Cron/PublishOutbox.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\OrderExport\Cron;

use Magento\Framework\App\ResourceConnection;
use Magento\Framework\MessageQueue\PublisherInterface;

class PublishOutbox
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly ResourceConnection $resource,
        private readonly PublisherInterface $publisher
    ) {
    }

    public function execute(): void
    {
        $connection = $this->resource->getConnection();
        $table = $this->resource->getTableName('maheshdave_order_outbox');
        $select = $connection->select()->from($table, ['order_id'])->where('status = ?', 'pending')->limit(100);
        foreach ($connection->fetchCol($select) as $orderId) {
            $this->publisher->publish('maheshdave.order.export', (string) $orderId);
            $connection->update($table, ['status' => 'queued'], ['order_id = ?' => (int) $orderId, 'status = ?' => 'pending']);
        }
    }
}

The update is conditional on status = pending so two cron processes cannot both publish the same row and both mark it. They can both publish if they read before either updates. The consumer must tolerate a duplicate order id, which it should anyway. If you need exactly-once publish, lock the row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE in a transaction. I have not needed it at this volume; the consumer's idempotency is the real guarantee, and the outbox is the guarantee that the message is not lost.

Mark the row sent in the consumer after the ERP accepts it, and failed with a last error after the final retry. A row that stays queued and never becomes sent is a consumer problem. A row that stays pending is a cron problem. Those are different pages in an incident, which is the reason for the two statuses.

Kill the process on purpose

Place an order. SELECT * FROM maheshdave_order_outbox WHERE order_id = ... shows pending even if you then kill the PHP-FPM worker. Run the cron. The row moves to queued and queue_message has the id. Run the consumer. The row moves to sent. If you only look at the ERP and not at this table, you will miss the orders sitting in failed, which is the queue you actually have to drain.

articles.title: Updating MSI Source Items in Bulk from an External Feed
articles.excerpt: A stock feed saved each SKU through the product repository and fought MSI reservations. SourceItemsSaveInterface updates the source item in bulk and leaves reservations to do their job.
articles.content:
The warehouse feed is a CSV of SKU, source code, and quantity. The first importer loaded each product and called setStockData and save. On a 50,000-row file it ran for hours, wrote the legacy stock item, and the salable quantity on the storefront did not match the file. MSI was enabled. Salable quantity is source quantity plus reservations. Writing the catalog stock item bypasses sources, and saving the product also fires everything else plugged into product save.

Magento\InventoryApi\Api\SourceItemsSaveInterface is the write API for source items. It accepts an array, so the batch size is yours to choose. I use 200. Larger batches make one failure reject a bigger set; smaller ones spend more time in PHP. Reservations are untouched, which is what you want: an open cart that reserved 2 units still reduces salable quantity after the source quantity is updated.

app/code/MaheshDave/StockFeed/Model/SourceItemImporter.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\StockFeed\Model;

use Magento\Framework\Api\DataObjectHelper;
use Magento\InventoryApi\Api\Data\SourceItemInterface;
use Magento\InventoryApi\Api\Data\SourceItemInterfaceFactory;
use Magento\InventoryApi\Api\SourceItemsSaveInterface;

class SourceItemImporter
{
    private const BATCH = 200;

    public function __construct(
        private readonly SourceItemsSaveInterface $sourceItemsSave,
        private readonly SourceItemInterfaceFactory $sourceItemFactory,
        private readonly DataObjectHelper $dataObjectHelper
    ) {
    }

    /**
     * @param array<int, array{sku: string, source_code: string, quantity: float}> $rows
     */
    public function import(array $rows): int
    {
        $saved = 0;
        foreach (array_chunk($rows, self::BATCH) as $chunk) {
            $items = [];
            foreach ($chunk as $row) {
                $item = $this->sourceItemFactory->create();
                $this->dataObjectHelper->populateWithArray($item, [
                    SourceItemInterface::SKU => (string) $row['sku'],
                    SourceItemInterface::SOURCE_CODE => (string) $row['source_code'],
                    SourceItemInterface::QUANTITY => (float) $row['quantity'],
                    SourceItemInterface::STATUS => ((float) $row['quantity']) > 0
                        ? SourceItemInterface::STATUS_IN_STOCK
                        : SourceItemInterface::STATUS_OUT_OF_STOCK,
                ], SourceItemInterface::class);
                $items[] = $item;
            }
            $this->sourceItemsSave->execute($items);
            $saved += count($items);
        }

        return $saved;
    }
}

Status is derived from quantity because a source item with quantity 0 and status in-stock still participates in odd ways in the salable calculation depending on version, and the feed does not send status. If the warehouse sends status explicitly, use theirs. Do not set quantity to 0 for a SKU that is simply absent from today's file. Absence means "the feed did not mention it", and zeroing those SKUs is how a partial file empties the catalog. The caller passes only the rows that were in the file.

This module sequences Magento_InventoryApi. It does nothing useful with MSI disabled, and it should not fall back to setStockData silently. If bin/magento module:status Magento_Inventory is disabled, stop and say so.

Salable quantity is not updated inside execute synchronously in a way you can read from a replica immediately. The inventory indexer runs. After a large import I run bin/magento indexer:reindex inventory if the storefront cannot wait for cron, and I do not run a full indexer:reindex because this change does not require the catalog product index.

Check source quantity and salable quantity separately

SELECT sku, source_code, quantity, status FROM inventory_source_item WHERE sku = '24-MB01';
SELECT sku, quantity FROM inventory_reservation WHERE sku = '24-MB01';

Source quantity matches the file. Reservations are whatever carts and orders already created; the import did not delete them. Salable quantity on the storefront is source quantity plus those reservation rows (they are stored negative). If you "fixed" a mismatch by deleting reservations, you oversell. If the source row did not change, the source code in the file is not a source Magento knows. inventory_source is the list. Inserting an unknown source code through this API fails the batch, which is preferable to creating a source by accident.

articles.seo_title: Bulk MSI Updates from a Stock Feed
articles.seo_description: Push an external stock feed through SourceItemsSaveInterface in batches. Per-SKU product saves ignore reservations and time out.

articles.title: Price Writes That Land in the Wrong Website
articles.excerpt: The price integration saved products in the admin store, so every website showed the US price. Product price is scoped per website only if you save it with that store's context.
articles.content:
The feed had one price per website. The importer called ProductRepositoryInterface::save() with the price set and no store context. Magento was in the admin store (store id 0). Website-scoped price attributes store the default value in that case, and every website that did not have an override showed the US price. The EU website override was never written. The API response looked successful.

A price attribute with website scope is stored in the attribute's value table with store_id 0 for the default and with the store id of each store view when overridden. Saving under the wrong store writes a row you did not intend, and the fallback logic then hides the bug: the website with no row shows default, so US looks correct and EU looks "not updated".

app/code/MaheshDave/PriceFeed/Model/WebsitePriceWriter.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\PriceFeed\Model;

use Magento\Catalog\Api\ProductRepositoryInterface;
use Magento\Framework\Exception\NoSuchEntityException;
use Magento\Store\Model\App\Emulation;
use Magento\Store\Model\StoreManagerInterface;

class WebsitePriceWriter
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly ProductRepositoryInterface $productRepository,
        private readonly StoreManagerInterface $storeManager,
        private readonly Emulation $emulation
    ) {
    }

    public function write(string $sku, string $storeCode, float $price): void
    {
        $store = $this->storeManager->getStore($storeCode);
        $this->emulation->startEnvironmentEmulation((int) $store->getId());
        try {
            $product = $this->productRepository->get($sku, true, (int) $store->getId(), true);
            $product->setPrice($price);
            $this->productRepository->save($product);
        } catch (NoSuchEntityException $e) {
            throw $e;
        } finally {
            $this->emulation->stopEnvironmentEmulation();
        }
    }
}

The third argument of get() is the store id used to load values. Edit mode true skips the flat in-memory cache of a product loaded for another store earlier in the same process. A long-running importer that does not pass the store id, and does not force reload, will save the first website's product over and over with a new price. I have shipped that bug. The finally stops emulation even when save throws, so the next SKU is not stuck in the EU store.

Emulation changes the current store for the whole process, including any plugin on save that calls getValue without a scope. That is what you want here and it is also why this code must not run inside a web request that still has to render another store. Run it from CLI. Do not call it from a storefront controller.

After the write, the price index is stale until catalog_product_price runs. The value you read back from the EAV table can be right while the storefront is wrong. Reindex that one indexer, or wait for schedule mode. Checking only the storefront is how this gets reported as "the save didn't work" an hour before cron.

The row that proves it

SELECT s.code, c.value
FROM catalog_product_entity_decimal c
JOIN eav_attribute a ON a.attribute_id = c.attribute_id AND a.attribute_code = 'price'
JOIN store s ON s.store_id = c.store_id
JOIN catalog_product_entity p ON p.entity_id = c.entity_id
WHERE p.sku = '24-MB01';

You want a row whose store code is the EU store view, not only admin / store id 0. One row at store id 0 means the writer never left the admin store. Then open the EU storefront only after the price indexer has run, or you will compare an indexed price with an EAV price and reopen the ticket.

articles.seo_description: A product save without the right store context writes the website-scoped price to default. Emulate the store, then save.

articles.title: Blocking Checkout for a Company That Is Not Approved
articles.excerpt: A company in pending status could still place an order because checkout only checks that the customer is logged in. Reject place order when CompanyInterface status is not approved.
articles.content:
Company approval was configured, and the company admin saw the pending state in their account. Checkout still placed the order. The approval workflow updates company.status. It does not, by itself, remove the customer's ability to call savePaymentInformationAndPlaceOrder. If the requirement is "no orders until sales approves the company", that check has to sit on the place-order service, because the storefront button is not the only caller. GraphQL placeOrder and a punchout integration hit the same service.

Magento\Company\Api\CompanyManagementInterface::getByCustomerId returns the company for a customer who belongs to one, and null for a retail customer. Retail must keep checking out. A null company is not a rejection. Magento\Company\Api\Data\CompanyInterface::STATUS_APPROVED is the status that is allowed to buy. Pending, rejected, and blocked are not.

savePaymentInformationAndPlaceOrder receives a cart id, not a customer id. Load the quote, then the company.

app/code/MaheshDave/CompanyGate/Plugin/RejectUnapprovedCompany.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\CompanyGate\Plugin;

use Magento\Checkout\Api\PaymentInformationManagementInterface;
use Magento\Company\Api\CompanyManagementInterface;
use Magento\Company\Api\Data\CompanyInterface;
use Magento\Framework\Exception\LocalizedException;
use Magento\Quote\Api\CartRepositoryInterface;

class RejectUnapprovedCompany
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly CompanyManagementInterface $companyManagement,
        private readonly CartRepositoryInterface $cartRepository
    ) {
    }

    public function beforeSavePaymentInformationAndPlaceOrder(
        PaymentInformationManagementInterface $subject,
        $cartId,
        $paymentMethod,
        $billingAddress = null
    ): array {
        $quote = $this->cartRepository->getActive((int) $cartId);
        $customerId = (int) $quote->getCustomerId();
        if ($customerId === 0) {
            return [$cartId, $paymentMethod, $billingAddress];
        }
        $company = $this->companyManagement->getByCustomerId($customerId);
        if ($company !== null && (int) $company->getStatus() !== CompanyInterface::STATUS_APPROVED) {
            throw new LocalizedException(__('This company is not approved to place orders.'));
        }

        return [$cartId, $paymentMethod, $billingAddress];
    }
}

A before plugin that returns null replaces the arguments with null on some versions. Return the original argument list. Guest checkout has customer id 0; do not look up a company for it. di.xml targets Magento\Checkout\Api\PaymentInformationManagementInterface. GraphQL place order on 2.4 goes through Magento\QuoteGraphQl and the payment method management path, not always this exact method. I verified the call stack on the project version before calling this done, and where GraphQL used Magento\Quote\Api\CartManagementInterface::placeOrder I put the same private check in a second plugin on that method. One plugin on the controller is not enough.

Company status is an integer column. Comparing it to the string approved never matches, and the plugin would reject every company, including approved ones. Use the constant. Log the status you saw when you throw, so a false reject is debuggable without reproducing the order.

The module sequence includes Magento_Company and Magento_Checkout. It is an Adobe Commerce B2B module. It will not install on Open Source, and it should not be in an Open Source package.

The two customers to try

A retail customer places an order. It succeeds. A customer whose company is pending gets the localized exception and no row in sales_order. Approve the company in the company admin and the same cart places. If the pending customer succeeds, the request did not pass through the interface you plugged. Turn on the debug log, place again, and see whether the plugin class is in the profiler. A preference on the checkout class that does not extend the interceptor will skip plugins entirely.

articles.seo_title: Stop Checkout for an Unapproved Company
articles.seo_description: Plug into Magento place order and refuse it when the B2B company exists and its status is not approved.

articles.title: Server-Side Validation for a Custom Checkout Field
articles.excerpt: The purchase-order number was validated in a Knockout rule. The ERP integration posted the cart through the API and stored an empty number. Validate it on the quote before place order.
articles.content:
The checkout step required a purchase-order number. The Knockout validation rule blocked the button. Finance then found orders with an empty number. Those orders had been placed by the customer's procurement tool, which calls PaymentInformationManagementInterface::savePaymentInformationAndPlaceOrder and never loads checkout/onepage. A UI rule is a convenience. The rule that matters reads the quote on the server.

Store the value as a quote extension attribute or a column on quote that sales converts to the order. I use a column maheshdave_po_number on quote and sales_order, declared in db_schema.xml, copied in a sales_model_service_quote_submit_before observer by $order->setData('maheshdave_po_number', $quote->getData('maheshdave_po_number')). Fieldset sales_convert_quote can do that copy too, when the field is in fieldset.xml. I use the observer when I want the copy to be obvious in code review.

app/code/MaheshDave/CheckoutPo/Plugin/RequirePoNumber.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\CheckoutPo\Plugin;

use Magento\Checkout\Api\PaymentInformationManagementInterface;
use Magento\Framework\Exception\InputException;
use Magento\Quote\Api\CartRepositoryInterface;

class RequirePoNumber
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly CartRepositoryInterface $cartRepository
    ) {
    }

    public function beforeSavePaymentInformationAndPlaceOrder(
        PaymentInformationManagementInterface $subject,
        $cartId,
        $paymentMethod,
        $billingAddress = null
    ): array {
        $quote = $this->cartRepository->getActive((int) $cartId);
        $poNumber = trim((string) $quote->getData('maheshdave_po_number'));
        if ($poNumber === '' || strlen($poNumber) > 40) {
            throw new InputException(__('Enter a purchase order number, 40 characters or fewer.'));
        }

        return [$cartId, $paymentMethod, $billingAddress];
    }
}

The payment plugin does not trust the request parameter. By the time place order runs, the number has to already be on the quote, written by a small repository method the checkout step and the procurement API both call. Validating $this->request->getParam('po_number') passes the browser, which posts the field, and still passes an API client that never sends it, because the param is simply absent and a careless if ($poNumber) was skipped. The quote is the document both clients share.

Save the number before payment, not in the same request as place order, unless that request's service sets it on the quote object and this plugin reads the object. A plugin that runs before the code which copies the param onto the quote will reject a valid browser checkout. I set the attribute in savePaymentInformation's before-plugin only when the payment additional data contains po_number, and the require-plugin reads whatever is on the quote after that. Order them with sortOrder. The writer is 10, the requirement is 20.

The client that does not use the browser

curl -s -X POST "https://example.test/rest/default/V1/carts/mine/payment-information" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"paymentMethod":{"method":"checkmo"},"billingAddress":{"email":"buyer@example.test","country_id":"US","street":["1 Main"],"telephone":"123","postcode":"10001","city":"NY","firstname":"A","lastname":"B"}}'

With an empty maheshdave_po_number on that quote, the response is an input exception and sales_order has no new row. Set the column on the quote, repeat, and the order's column matches. The Knockout rule can stay. It is not the test. The curl is the test. Admin reorder and negotiable-quote acceptance do not call this method. If those paths must require the same number, put the same check on the service they call and keep the exception text identical.
