articles.seo_title: Validate a Checkout Field on the Server
articles.seo_description: A Knockout rule does not run for REST or GraphQL checkout. Require the purchase-order number on the quote in a before-place-order plugin.

articles.title: An around Plugin That Called proceed() Twice
articles.excerpt: An around plugin logged the duration of place order by calling proceed(), then called proceed() again in a branch that was not supposed to run. Customers got two orders. Around is the wrong tool unless you need to skip the call.
articles.content:
Duplicate orders, same quote, two increment ids, a few hundred milliseconds apart. The payment gateway showed one capture. The second order had no capture and a processing status that nothing could fulfill. The audit of plugins on PaymentInformationManagementInterface::savePaymentInformationAndPlaceOrder found an around plugin whose job was to log how long placement took. The happy path called $proceed, logged, and returned. A catch block called $proceed again because the author thought the first call had not counted after an exception. Exceptions from $proceed mean the call happened. A second call places a second order if the first one committed, and throws a quote-is-not-active error if it did not. Both happened, depending on timing.

Logging does not need around

after runs only if the method returned. You lose the duration of failures. That is a bad trade if you are building a metric, and it is the right trade if a mistake in the metric code can place an order. I log duration from the New Relic transaction instead, and the plugin that remains is after for a result I need to change. When I do write around, $proceed is called once, on one line, and the result is what I return.

app/code/MaheshDave/DevTools/Plugin/PlaceOrderTiming.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\DevTools\Plugin;

use Magento\Checkout\Api\PaymentInformationManagementInterface;
use Psr\Log\LoggerInterface;

class PlaceOrderTiming
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly LoggerInterface $logger
    ) {
    }

    public function aroundSavePaymentInformationAndPlaceOrder(
        PaymentInformationManagementInterface $subject,
        callable $proceed,
        $cartId,
        $paymentMethod,
        $billingAddress = null
    ) {
        $started = microtime(true);
        try {
            $orderId = $proceed($cartId, $paymentMethod, $billingAddress);
        } catch (\Throwable $e) {
            $this->logger->error('place order failed', [
                'cart_id' => $cartId,
                'ms' => (int) ((microtime(true) - $started) * 1000),
                'error' => $e->getMessage(),
            ]);
            throw $e;
        }
        $this->logger->info('place order finished', [
            'cart_id' => $cartId,
            'order_id' => $orderId,
            'ms' => (int) ((microtime(true) - $started) * 1000),
        ]);

        return $orderId;
    }
}

One $proceed. The catch logs and rethrows the same exception. It does not call the gateway again. Returning a new exception instead of throwing the original one drops the stack and can convert a LocalizedException the storefront knows how to print into a generic 500. Rethrow.

around is the plugin type that can skip the original method by not calling $proceed. That is the only reason I reach for it: a feature flag that returns a cached result, or a guard that throws before any side effect. An around that always calls $proceed and only adds behavior before or after is an before plus an after, and those cannot run the original method twice. Code review on this class is the question "how many times is $proceed invoked on each path", including paths added in a later pull request. I have rejected a "retry" branch here. Retry of place order belongs in the client, with a new idempotency key, not in a plugin that shares the same quote.

Seeing a double call before production

Add the plugin, place one order, and count rows:

SELECT entity_id, increment_id, created_at FROM sales_order WHERE quote_id = 4242;

One row. Temporarily throw after $proceed in a dev branch and confirm the log line says failed and that a retry of the HTTP request is what creates the second order, not the catch block. If the catch block creates it, $proceed is in there. The log line alone is not the test. The row count is.
articles.author: Mahesh Dave
articles.seo_title: The around Plugin That Ran Twice
articles.seo_description: Calling proceed() twice in a Magento around plugin places two orders. Use after for logging, and call proceed() once.

articles.title: A Read-Only Health Command for Magento Diagnostics
articles.excerpt: Deployment checks were a page of bin/magento commands everyone ran differently. devtools:health prints indexer backlog, invalid caches, and recent cron errors as JSON, and it does not change anything.
articles.content:
After a deploy, three people ran three different checks. One reindexed. One flushed cache. One looked at cron. The reindex and the flush were not checks, and they hid the actual failure. The command I want on a deploy pipeline is read-only, exits non-zero when something is wrong, and prints JSON so the pipeline can store it. It lives in MaheshDave_DevTools because it is operational tooling, not a feature of the catalog.

app/code/MaheshDave/DevTools/Console/Command/HealthCommand.php

<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace MaheshDave\DevTools\Console\Command;

use Magento\Cron\Model\ResourceModel\Schedule\CollectionFactory as ScheduleCollectionFactory;
use Magento\Framework\App\Cache\TypeListInterface;
use Magento\Indexer\Model\Indexer\CollectionFactory as IndexerCollectionFactory;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Command\Command;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Input\InputInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Output\OutputInterface;

class HealthCommand extends Command
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly IndexerCollectionFactory $indexerCollectionFactory,
        private readonly TypeListInterface $cacheTypeList,
        private readonly ScheduleCollectionFactory $scheduleCollectionFactory
    ) {
        parent::__construct();
    }

    protected function configure(): void
    {
        $this->setName('devtools:health');
        $this->setDescription('Read-only indexer, cache, and cron status as JSON');
    }

    protected function execute(InputInterface $input, OutputInterface $output): int
    {
        $indexers = [];
        $indexerBad = false;
        foreach ($this->indexerCollectionFactory->create() as $indexer) {
            $backlog = $indexer->getState()->getStatus();
            $indexers[] = [
                'id' => $indexer->getId(),
                'status' => $backlog,
                'scheduled' => $indexer->isScheduled(),
            ];
            if ($backlog !== 'valid') {
                $indexerBad = true;
            }
        }

        $invalidCaches = [];
        foreach ($this->cacheTypeList->getInvalidated() as $type) {
            $invalidCaches[] = $type->getId();
        }

        $errors = [];
        $schedules = $this->scheduleCollectionFactory->create();
        $schedules->addFieldToFilter('status', 'error');
        $schedules->setOrder('scheduled_at', 'DESC');
        $schedules->setPageSize(5);
        foreach ($schedules as $schedule) {
            $errors[] = [
                'job' => $schedule->getJobCode(),
                'at' => $schedule->getScheduledAt(),
                'message' => mb_substr((string) $schedule->getMessages(), 0, 240),
            ];
        }

        $report = [
            'indexers' => $indexers,
            'invalid_caches' => $invalidCaches,
            'recent_cron_errors' => $errors,
        ];
        $output->writeln((string) json_encode($report, JSON_PRETTY_PRINT));

        return ($indexerBad || $invalidCaches !== [] || $errors !== []) ? Command::FAILURE : Command::SUCCESS;
    }
}

Register it on Magento\Framework\Console\CommandListInterface in etc/di.xml with an item of type object pointing at this class. The command does not call cache:flush, does not reindex, and does not change indexer mode. getInvalidated() and the indexer state are reads. Cron errors are reads of cron_schedule. Exit code 1 is a failed check, not an exception. A pipeline that treats any non-zero as "deploy failed" should decide whether a single old cron error from yesterday is enough to fail the deploy. I fail on it and I delete or age out rows so yesterday's error does not block today's release. If you only want errors since the deploy started, filter scheduled_at with a from option. I did not add the option until a team asked, because a command with five flags becomes the page of commands this replaced.

Indexer status working during the deploy window fails the check even when the indexer is healthy and simply running. Run the command after setup:upgrade has finished and cron has had a cycle, not in the middle of it. scheduled: false on a catalog indexer in production is the finding I care about more than invalid, because an indexer left on save after a debug session will lock product saves. The JSON includes the flag. The exit code does not fail on it yet; I print it so a human sees it. Failing the deploy because one custom indexer is on save has cried wolf on every project where that indexer has no mview.

Run it

bin/magento devtools:health
echo $?

The output is a JSON object with indexers, invalid_caches, and recent_cron_errors. Exit 0 means every indexer reported valid, no cache type was invalidated, and cron_schedule had no error rows in the five most recent errors, meaning none. Exit 1 is a reason to look at the JSON, not a reason to flush. If the command itself is missing, setup:di:compile has not picked up the CommandListInterface argument, or the module is disabled.
articles.author: Mahesh Dave
articles.seo_title: A Read-Only Magento Health Command
articles.seo_description: MaheshDave_DevTools adds devtools:health, a read-only JSON report of indexer mode, cache status, and cron errors.

articles.title: How to Remove a Fastly VCL Snippet Using CLI
articles.excerpt: Remove a custom Fastly VCL snippet that locks you out of Magento admin by cloning the active version, deleting the snippet, validating, and activating through the API or CLI.
articles.content:
When a custom Fastly VCL snippet blocks Magento admin access (for example Maintenance_Trigger), you can remove it safely using the Fastly API and curl — without Magento admin or the Fastly web UI.

This guide covers:

  1. Backing up existing VCL snippets
  2. Removing a specific snippet
  3. Activating the new VCL version
  4. Purging Fastly cache

Prerequisites

ItemDescription
Fastly Service IDFastly dashboard → Service configuration, or Magento Cloud FASTLY_SERVICE_ID
Fastly API TokenFastly dashboard → Account → API tokens (snippet edit + purge permissions)
Snippet nameExact name, e.g. Maintenance_Trigger
Toolscurl, bash, optionally python3 or jq

Important: Fastly version rules

You cannot edit an active (locked) version directly.

Workflow:

  1. Clone the active version
  2. Delete the snippet on the cloned draft
  3. Validate the new version
  4. Activate the new version
  5. Purge cache

Step 1 — Set environment variables

export FASTLY_SERVICE_ID="YOUR_SERVICE_ID_HERE"
export FASTLY_API_TOKEN="YOUR_API_TOKEN_HERE"
export SNIPPET_NAME="Maintenance_Trigger"
export BACKUP_DIR="./fastly-vcl-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"

mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"
echo "Backup directory: $BACKUP_DIR"

Step 2 — Get the active VCL version

curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/active" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json"

cat "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json"

Extract the active version number:

export ACTIVE_VERSION=$(grep -o '"number":[0-9]*' "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json" | head -1 | cut -d: -f2)
echo "Active version: $ACTIVE_VERSION"

Alternative (Python):

export ACTIVE_VERSION=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json'))['number'])")
echo "Active version: $ACTIVE_VERSION"

Alternative (jq):

export ACTIVE_VERSION=$(jq -r '.number' "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json")
echo "Active version: $ACTIVE_VERSION"

Note: Use -o to save JSON. Do not use curl -w with JSON files — it appends HTTP_STATUS:200 and breaks JSON parsing.

Step 3 — Backup all VCL snippets

curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$ACTIVE_VERSION/snippet" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/all-snippets-active-v${ACTIVE_VERSION}.json"

cat "$BACKUP_DIR/all-snippets-active-v${ACTIVE_VERSION}.json"

List all snippet names:

grep -o '"name":"[^"]*"' "$BACKUP_DIR/all-snippets-active-v${ACTIVE_VERSION}.json"

Confirm target snippet exists:

grep -i "$SNIPPET_NAME" "$BACKUP_DIR/all-snippets-active-v${ACTIVE_VERSION}.json"

Step 4 — Backup the specific snippet

curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$ACTIVE_VERSION/snippet/$SNIPPET_NAME" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/${SNIPPET_NAME}-active-v${ACTIVE_VERSION}.json"

cat "$BACKUP_DIR/${SNIPPET_NAME}-active-v${ACTIVE_VERSION}.json"

Save VCL content to a .vcl file (optional):

python3 - <<'PY'
import json, os

backup_dir = os.environ["BACKUP_DIR"]
snippet = os.environ["SNIPPET_NAME"]
version = os.environ["ACTIVE_VERSION"]
path = f"{backup_dir}/{snippet}-active-v{version}.json"

data = json.load(open(path))
out = f"{backup_dir}/{snippet}.vcl"

with open(out, "w") as f:
    f.write(data.get("content", ""))

print(f"Saved: {out}")
PY

Step 5 — Clone the active version

curl -sS -X PUT -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$ACTIVE_VERSION/clone" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/cloned-version.json"

cat "$BACKUP_DIR/cloned-version.json"

Set the new draft version:

export NEW_VERSION=$(grep -o '"number":[0-9]*' "$BACKUP_DIR/cloned-version.json" | head -1 | cut -d: -f2)
echo "New draft version: $NEW_VERSION"

Step 6 — Delete the snippet from cloned version

curl -sS -X DELETE -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$NEW_VERSION/snippet/$SNIPPET_NAME" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/delete-snippet-response.json"

cat "$BACKUP_DIR/delete-snippet-response.json"

Verify snippet is removed:

curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$NEW_VERSION/snippet" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/all-snippets-new-v${NEW_VERSION}.json"

grep -i "$SNIPPET_NAME" "$BACKUP_DIR/all-snippets-new-v${NEW_VERSION}.json" \
  || echo "Snippet removed successfully"

Step 7 — Validate VCL before activation

curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$NEW_VERSION/validate" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/validate.json"

cat "$BACKUP_DIR/validate.json"

Confirm status is ok before activating. Do not activate if validation fails.

Step 8 — Activate the new VCL version

curl -sS -X PUT -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$NEW_VERSION/activate" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/activate.json"

cat "$BACKUP_DIR/activate.json"

Step 9 — Purge Fastly cache

curl -sS -X POST -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/purge_all" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/purge.json"

cat "$BACKUP_DIR/purge.json"

Step 10 — Verify admin access

Open Magento admin in a private/incognito window:

https://your-domain.com/admin

Complete one-shot script

Save as remove-fastly-snippet.sh:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

export FASTLY_SERVICE_ID="YOUR_SERVICE_ID_HERE"
export FASTLY_API_TOKEN="YOUR_API_TOKEN_HERE"
export SNIPPET_NAME="Maintenance_Trigger"
export BACKUP_DIR="./fastly-vcl-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"

mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"

echo "==> 1) Get active version"
curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/active" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json"

export ACTIVE_VERSION=$(grep -o '"number":[0-9]*' "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json" | head -1 | cut -d: -f2)
echo "    Active version: $ACTIVE_VERSION"

echo "==> 2) Backup all snippets"
curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$ACTIVE_VERSION/snippet" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/all-snippets-active-v${ACTIVE_VERSION}.json"

echo "==> 3) Backup target snippet"
curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$ACTIVE_VERSION/snippet/$SNIPPET_NAME" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/${SNIPPET_NAME}-active-v${ACTIVE_VERSION}.json"

echo "==> 4) Clone version"
curl -sS -X PUT -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$ACTIVE_VERSION/clone" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/cloned-version.json"

export NEW_VERSION=$(grep -o '"number":[0-9]*' "$BACKUP_DIR/cloned-version.json" | head -1 | cut -d: -f2)
echo "    New version: $NEW_VERSION"

echo "==> 5) Delete snippet"
curl -sS -X DELETE -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$NEW_VERSION/snippet/$SNIPPET_NAME" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/delete-snippet-response.json"

echo "==> 6) Validate"
curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$NEW_VERSION/validate" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/validate.json"
cat "$BACKUP_DIR/validate.json"

echo "==> 7) Activate"
curl -sS -X PUT -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/$NEW_VERSION/activate" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/activate.json"

echo "==> 8) Purge cache"
curl -sS -X POST -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/purge_all" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/purge.json"

echo "Done. Backups saved in: $BACKUP_DIR"

Make executable and run:

chmod +x remove-fastly-snippet.sh
./remove-fastly-snippet.sh

Troubleshooting

FileNotFoundError: active-version.json

Backup file was not created. Re-run Step 2 and confirm BACKUP_DIR is set in the same shell.

echo "BACKUP_DIR=${BACKUP_DIR:-NOT_SET}"
ls -la "${BACKUP_DIR:-missing}"

JSONDecodeError: Extra data

curl -w appended HTTP_STATUS:200 after JSON. Re-fetch cleanly:

curl -sS -H "Fastly-Key: $FASTLY_API_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/version/active" \
  -o "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json"

Or fix existing file:

head -n 1 "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json" > /tmp/active-version.clean.json
mv /tmp/active-version.clean.json "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json"

Validate JSON:

python3 -m json.tool "$BACKUP_DIR/active-version.json"

Invalid credentials

{"msg":"Provided credentials are missing or invalid"}

Check FASTLY_API_TOKEN and regenerate if needed.

Service or snippet not found

{"msg":"Record not found"}

Verify FASTLY_SERVICE_ID and snippet name (case-sensitive):

grep -o '"name":"[^"]*"' "$BACKUP_DIR/all-snippets-active-v${ACTIVE_VERSION}.json"

# Purge again

  "https://api.fastly.com/service/$FASTLY_SERVICE_ID/purge_all"

bin/magento maintenance:status

Best practices

  • Always back up before deleting snippets
  • Validate VCL before activation
  • Keep the backup directory until admin access is confirmed
  • Never commit API tokens to git
  • Use incognito/private window when testing admin after changes

Applicable to Adobe Commerce / Magento 2 with Fastly CDN (fastly/magento2 module).

Key takeaways

  • Active Fastly versions are immutable—always clone before deleting snippets.
  • Validate VCL before activation; keep JSON backups until admin access is confirmed.
  • Pair CDN changes with Magento maintenance checks (var/maintenance.flag) when admin stays blocked.
